text:
The finest Black-owned barbershop in the South would not cut a Black man's hair, and it held that line until 1965. Every barber in Alonzo Herndon's shop was Black. Every customer in the chairs was white, because a white man in Georgia would not sit where a Black man had sat.

He had a brush in his hand and a man's shoe in front of him.

That is what he was doing, not walking home, not out on the street where the trouble was, not anywhere he had chosen to be.

He was at work, kneeling at a stand in a barbershop, shining a stranger's shoes for a dime.

He heard it before he saw it. Every man in that shop did, the barbers with their razors still up, the customers half lathered, the whole room going quiet the way a room does.

Then they came through the door.

They took him out into the street and beat him to death there, in front of the shop, while the city watched.

He was a boy. The one journalist who went to Atlanta afterward and did the work described him as lame, industrious, and at that moment actually shining a man's shoes.

That journalist never got his name. Neither did anybody else writing that week.

It was Saturday, the twenty-second of September, 1906, and the address was 66 Peachtree Street.

The shop belonged to Alonzo Herndon. It was the largest barbershop in Atlanta and one of the most famous in the American South, and every barber working in it was Black, and every customer sitting in it was white.

That was not an accident and it was not a compromise. It was the entire business model, and it went back further than Herndon did.

Before the Civil War, barbering was one of the few skilled trades a Black man in America was permitted to hold. It was permitted precisely because it was performed on white bodies.

Enslavers hired out enslaved barbers by the day and pocketed the fee. The work was indoors, out of the sun, out of the field, and for a man with no other door open to him it was the best of a set of terrible options.

Free Black barbers did not escape that arrangement after emancipation. They built on it.

They served white men only, because white men held the money in the South and because a shop that took both would lose the white trade inside a week. There was a second reason, and nobody printed it on a sign.

A white customer would not sit in a chair that had held a Black man. He would not take a razor that had touched a Black face, or shears that had been through Black hair.

So the finest Black-owned businesses in the South were businesses their own people were barred from. A Black man in Atlanta with money in his pocket could not get a haircut at the best Black barbershop in the city.

The historian Quincy Mills has written that what these men were selling was never only a shave. They were staging, every morning, the exact arrangement of bodies the South needed to believe in.

And doing it with an open razor at the throat of every man who believed it. Ten and twelve times a day, forty years running, in a country where a Black man could be killed on a rumor.

Ray Stannard Baker, the journalist, came to Atlanta a few months after the massacre and sat in the dining room of the Piedmont Hotel. He noticed that white men at his table talked about the race question at full volume with Black waiters standing right there, and he asked one of his companions whether the men were sensitive to it.

His companion said they never minded them, that they did not care. One of the waiters spoke up immediately and told the table not to mind him, that he was only a block of wood.

That was the product, and it was never the haircut.

It was the block of wood.

Alonzo Herndon walked out of Social Circle, Georgia in 1878 with eleven dollars and about a year of schooling behind him. He had been born into slavery in Walton County in 1858, the son of the white man who owned his mother, a man who never claimed him.

He learned to cut hair in Senoia and opened his first shop in Jonesboro, not Atlanta. He reached Atlanta in the early 1880s, bought half of another Black man's shop on Marietta Street, and by 1904 he owned three barbershops in the city.

Three. Not the hundred that gets passed around online every February.

By 1907 Baker put his worth at eighty thousand dollars, with some fifty houses that he rented out. All of it earned after slavery, by a man who had reached twenty with one year of school.

He had a method and he stated it plainly. Careful work, and conduct so tactful and polite that no white customer could ever take offense.

A Black newspaper in Atlanta later summed up his position without much affection, saying he believed he did more for the race by making jobs for them than by arguing about the race problem. He employed seventy-five barbers over the course of his life and refused every offer to sell the shop, which is one way of reading what he thought he was doing.

The bargain was simple and every man in the trade understood it, which was to be indispensable, gentle and invisible.

Handle the throats of the most powerful men in Georgia every day of your life, and give them no reason, ever, to think of you as anything but useful.

The men holding up their end of it were judges, bankers, ministers and legislators, the top of white Atlanta. The men who came through the door on the night it was tested were not.

The city had four daily newspapers that year and they were in a circulation war. All summer they had run accounts of Black men attacking white women, and Baker later had every one of those cases personally investigated.

Of the four alleged assaults the papers screamed about that afternoon, his investigation found two that may have been attempts and two that were nothing at all. In one, an elderly white woman closing her blinds saw a Black man on the sidewalk, screamed, and telephoned the police, then telephoned back to tell them not to come.

That was one of the assaults printed in letters five inches high.

It was a hot Saturday half holiday, with the country people in town, the streets full, and the saloons on Decatur Street open since morning.

The Atlanta News put out five separate extras. Newsboys ran them through the crowd shouting third assault, fourth assault.

By nine that evening several thousand white men and boys had gathered at Five Points, a great many of them armed, because Atlanta was a city where the pawnshop windows looked like arsenals.

They started with a Black messenger boy on a bicycle. After that they stopped making distinctions.

They pulled riders off the streetcars and threw them through the windows. One woman was pushed out of a car window, dragged across the sidewalk by her leg, and thrown through a shop window.

They went into the Kimball House and the other good hotels and dragged the Black staff out into the street. A Western Union messenger named Frank Smith, eighteen years old, was caught near the Forsyth Street bridge and thrown off it.

Then they went into the barbershops.

They did not go looking for anyone in particular. They went into the rooms where Black men were at that moment shaving white customers and pulled them out of their chairs.

Alonzo Herndon had closed early and gone home. His windows came in and his fittings were destroyed, and across the street a second barbershop was raided and the barbers in it were killed.

Inside Herndon's shop they found the boy at the stand.

Later that night the mob carried three of the dead to the base of the Henry Grady statue on Marietta Street and laid them there, at the monument to the newspaperman who had spent his career assuring the country that the South had settled its race question.

A man named Milton Brown was shot three times on Peters Street with Atlanta police officers watching. While he waited for an ambulance that did not reach him in time, he said he knew nothing of the trouble going on.

Two nights later the violence moved out to Brownsville, a settlement south of the city where nearly every Black family owned its own house. There were two colleges there, a post office run by a Black postmaster, three churches and no saloon.

The county police went in, a gun battle started in the dark, and among the dead was George Wilder, seventy years old, who had escaped slavery during the Civil War and enlisted in the Union Army. His headstone in South-View Cemetery carries the middle name he took because of that service, Union, and a hand-lettered line saying he was killed in the riot.

The following Tuesday the frightened white leadership of Atlanta gathered in the courthouse to work out how to stop it.

In the middle of that meeting a Black man stood up, uncertainly.

It was Dr. W. F. Penn, one of the leading physicians in the city and a Yale man.

Every white man in that room knew him, because he had treated their families.

He told them that a mob had come to his house the day before. Ten white men had been sent inside to search for weapons, and his small daughter had run from one to the next, catching at them, begging them not to shoot her father.

Then he asked them a question that the men who heard it said left the room completely silent. He wanted to know the requirements under which a Black man in Atlanta could live and be protected.

He had done everything, sober and industrious and professional, a property owner raising his children carefully, treating the white families of that very city.

He asked them to tell him what the standard was, because he had met every standard he knew of and a mob had still come up his walk.

Nobody in that room had an answer, which is the answer.

There was no standard, and there never had been one.

That is the thing the barbershop was built to disprove, and the barbershop is where the disproving happened.

When the meeting turned practical, the white men of Atlanta passed the hat. They raised four thousand four hundred and twenty-three dollars for the Black victims of the riot, and the city later added a thousand more.

Set that against the twelve dead and the roughly seventy wounded the official committee counted, and against the eighty thousand dollars one Black barber in that city was worth.

The committee's own report is worth reading, because two white men wrote it honestly and it does not flinch. Not one of the mob's victims was a vagrant, it says.

Every one of them had been earning wages in useful work up to the moment they were attacked. Most of the dead left small children and widows with almost no money and almost no way to earn any.

The wounded lost between one and eight weeks of work, at fifty cents to four dollars a day each. And since dozens of men had taken part in each attack, the report concluded that several hundred murderers were walking around the city unbothered.

Nobody was ever convicted of killing any of them.

About a thousand Black people left Atlanta after that weekend. Hoke Smith took the governorship he had campaigned for and delivered the literacy test that kept most Black Georgians from voting for the next fifty years.

Black businesses were pushed out of the downtown commercial district by ordinance and by pressure, and drifted east to Auburn Avenue. Baker, walking Atlanta a few months later, found separate elevators, separate saloons, separate Bibles in the courtroom, and a public library no Black taxpayer was allowed to enter.

He also met a Black druggist named Moses Amos who had once thought about leaving the South for good. Amos went north to look it over and the first thing he wanted was a shave.

He walked the streets of that Northern city for two hours, going into barbershop after barbershop, and every one of them found a reason to turn him away. He finally gave up, bought a razor, and shaved himself.

Then he came home to Atlanta and stayed.

Herndon rebuilt. In 1913 he put twelve thousand dollars into the shop at 66 Peachtree and reopened it as the Crystal Palace, and there has never been anything like it before or since in the trade.

The doors were mahogany and beveled plate glass, sixteen feet tall. The ceiling was white pressed tin, the floor white ceramic tile, the walls hung with French beveled mirrors under crystal chandeliers.

Twenty-three custom chairs ran the length of the room in dark green Spanish leather, fitted out in porcelain, brass and nickel. Everything in my shop is the best procurable, Herndon told a reporter, and he meant every word of it as advertising.

Twenty baths and showers waited on the lower level. A quarter bought you one, a quarter bought a haircut, a dime bought a shave, forty cents got your suit pressed while you sat there in it.

A dime bought a shine.

The barbers worked eight in the morning to eight at night, midnight on Saturdays, in white linen changed every day. They were expected to come to work through the back, because that was the custom for Black employees on Peachtree Street, and Herndon had a second set of mahogany doors installed on the Broad Street side so his own men would not enter the building like freight.

And the shoeshine stands in that room were made of nickel and marble.

A newspaper printed that. Somebody stood in the doorway of the finest barbershop in the South, took in the chandeliers and the mirrors and the green leather, and thought the shoeshine stands were worth a line of their own.

The metal and the stone.

Seven years after a boy was dragged off one of those stands and into the street.

The trade held on at that address for another sixty years, and it held the color line the entire time.

In late November of 1965, fourteen demonstrators from Dr. King's Southern Christian Leadership Conference walked into the shop and sat down in every chair in the room.

They asked for haircuts. The Black barbers refused them, and the standoff ran four days before the owner gave in.

Jet covered it that December. One of the first Black men into those chairs was Julian Bond, freshly elected to the Georgia legislature and about to be refused his seat in it.

In the summer of 1973 the shop cut its last head of hair. A haircut cost two dollars and twenty-five cents by then.

Shave or shine, extra.

Alonzo Herndon died the wealthiest Black man in Atlanta. He has a fifteen-room mansion on University Place you can walk through by appointment, a plaza on Auburn Avenue, a state historical marker, a foundation, and an insurance company still trading under his name a century later.

He earned every bit of it, out of eleven dollars and one year of school, and nobody should take a dollar of it off him.

The boy at the stand has nickel and marble.

Somebody stood in that doorway and thought the metal and the stone were worth a line of their own. Nobody standing there that night took down what the boy was called.

One name has been attached to him since, in a documentary made in 2023, and it is Henry Welch. The city's own memorial project lists a William or Henry Welch separately, as a barber of about thirty who was shot and left to die near Grady Hospital, on the other side of downtown.

Which is not what happened at 66 Peachtree Street, to a boy who was on his knees with a brush in his hand.

The record cannot hold two dead Black men apart well enough to say which one of them this was. That is the actual condition of the paperwork, and it is worth knowing before anybody tells you the history has been settled.

At least twenty-five Black Atlantans were killed that weekend and the real figure runs higher. Eleven were never identified at all.

That number is not fixed, and this is the part I want you to have. In September 2023, researchers from the Truth and Transformation Initiative, Emory University's Georgia Civil Rights Cold Cases Project and the Afro-American Historical and Genealogical Society stood at the base of the Grady statue and announced they had pulled two more names out of Fulton County death records.

Stinson Ferguson, twenty-five years old. And Marshall Carter, thirteen, written on the form as a schoolboy.

A hundred and seventeen years later, and the paperwork still gave up two of them. It can give up more.

So when somebody tells you that Black money in this country came out of nothing but hustle, give them the address. Sixty-six Peachtree Street, a quarter a head, in the most beautiful room in Georgia, where every man working the floor was Black and not one of them was allowed to sit down in it.

And tell them there is still a boy on that floor with a shoe brush in his hand, and the people going through the death forms have not reached him yet.

Not yet.

Vatican Dispatch
On Good Friday, Pope Leo speaks with presidents of Israel and Ukraine, calling for an end to war
by Gerard O’Connell
April 3, 2026

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy greets Pope Leo XIV during a meeting at the papal residence in Castel Gandolfo Dec. 9, 2025. Pope Leo spoke over the telephone with both Zelenskyy and Israeli President Isaac Herzog April 3, 2026, Good Friday, urging diplomatic solutions and humanitarian support amid the ongoing wars in the Middle East and Europe. (CNS photo/Vatican Media)
Pope Leo XIV spoke about the need to end the wars in the Middle East and in Ukraine in phone conversations with the presidents of Israel and Ukraine on this Good Friday morning, April 3.

The Vatican issued press statements revealing that the pope had spoken with the presidents separately. Following the Vatican’s usual diplomatic protocol, the statements did not share who initiated the conversations, but America has learned from an informed Vatican source that the conversations were initiated by the Israeli and Ukrainian sides.

After Leo’s conversation with the Israeli president Isaac Herzog, the Vatican issued a brief and concise statement.

“This morning, April 3, a phone call took place between the Holy Father Leo XIV and Mr. Isaac Herzog, President of the State of Israel, on the occasion of the paschal festivities.”

This year Catholics and Jews are celebrating the paschal feasts around the same time. Jews celebrate the feast of Pesach (Passover) this year, the 5,786th year in the Hebrew calendar; the feast began at sundown on April 1 and will end at nightfall on April 8. Catholics, on the other hand, follow the Gregorian calendar and therefore celebrate Easter (the paschal feast) on Sunday, April 5, while Orthodox Christians, who follow the Julian calendar, will celebrate on April 12.

Significantly, the Vatican statement said that, on the call between Pope Leo and President Herzog, “the need to reopen all possible channels of diplomatic dialogue was reiterated, to put an end to the serious conflict underway, with a view to a just and lasting peace throughout the Middle East.”

Ever since Israel and the United States launched the war against Iran on Feb. 28, Pope Leo has repeatedly called publicly for an end to the conflict and has emphasized the need to open negotiations through dialogue. He did so again last Tuesday evening, March 31, at Castel Gandolfo, the papal summer residence. Responding to a question from CNN, he said he hopes President Donald Trump is looking for “an off ramp” to end the war with Iran and “for a way to decrease the amount of violence, of bombing, which would be a significant contribution to removing the hatred that’s being created and that’s increasing constantly in the Middle East and elsewhere.”

Leo then added, “I would certainly continue to give this call to all leaders of the world and say, come back to the table to dialogue. Let’s look for solutions to problems. Let’s look for ways to reduce the amount of violence that we’re promoting. That peace, especially at Easter, might reign in our hearts.”

In this morning’s conversation with Israel’s president, the Vatican said they also spoke about “the importance of protecting the civilian population and promoting respect for international and humanitarian law.” Pope Leo strongly emphasized the urgent need for this in his January 9 speech to the ambassadors from the 184 countries that have diplomatic relations with the Holy See, and lamented the fact that it is not happening. Indeed countries, including those engaged in the Iran war, are undermining these laws.

President Herzog, who attended Leo’s papal inauguration on May 18, 2025, and has also spoken with the pope by phone, revealed more about his conversation with the pope, and from Israel’s particular perspective. This is clear from the statement released by the President Herzog’s spokesperson at about the same time the Vatican press statement was released. The Israeli statement specifically mentions both Iran and Lebanon, a country the pope visited late last year, where Israel has again launched a military offensive against Hezbollah in reprisal for the latter’s attack against Israel and is seeking to take control of part of southern Lebanon.

According to the Israeli president’s spokesperson:

“On April 3, 2026, President Isaac Herzog spoke with His Holiness, Pope Leo XIV, to exchange greetings for the Passover and Easter holidays. President Herzog extended his warmest wishes for the Easter holiday to Christian communities across the Middle East and around the world.

“During their call, they discussed the war with Iran, including the ongoing threat of missile attacks by the Iranian regime and its terror proxies against people of all faiths in the region. President Herzog recalled the recent Iranian missile attacks on Jerusalem that fell in the area of sites holy to Christians, Muslims, and Jews.

“They also spoke about the situation in Lebanon, including the importance of the safety and security of Christian communities on both sides of the border. President Herzog emphasized that the Hezbollah terror organization cannot be allowed to continue threatening both the people of Israel and Lebanon, who both deserve a future of peace and stability.

“President Herzog expressed to Pope Leo XIV the great importance of the State of Israel’s relationship with the Holy See, the Catholic Church, and Christians around the world. He also underscored the importance of the cooperation of all world and religious leaders in the crucial fight against antisemitism.

“They expressed their shared hope for a more peaceful future for people of all faiths across the world, free from the threat of violence and bloodshed.”

It is perhaps noteworthy that there is no mention in either the Vatican or the Israeli statement of the tensions produced on Palm Sunday when Israeli police prevented the Latin Patriarch of Jerusalem, Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa, from entering the Basilica of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem. President Herzog intervened directly to help ease these tensions, following negative reactions in many countries. Since then, the Israeli government has ensured that Cardinal Pizzaballa will have full access to the basilica for religious services during Holy Week. Presumably both sides consider the problem closed.

This Good Friday evening, Pope Leo will visit Rome’s Coliseum and carry the cross for all fourteen Stations of the Cross, and the accompanying meditations, written by an Italian Franciscan priest, Francesco Patton, who lived many years in the Holy Land, and will focus on the fact that the world today is experiencing “The Way of the Cross.”

Pope speaks with Ukraine’s President

In a second press statement today, the Vatican revealed that Pope Leo and Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelensky had again spoken by phone this Good Friday morning. The two leaders have already had three face-to-face conversations and have also spoken together by phone.

The Vatican described the conversation as “cordial” and said “the Holy Father expressed his good wishes on the occasion of the Easter festivities, reaffirming his closeness to the Ukrainian people.”

The statement said, “The humanitarian situation was then discussed, reiterating the urgency of ensuring the necessary aid to the population tried by the conflict.” The war began 1,500 days ago on Feb. 24, 2022, when President Putin ordered Russian forces to invade Ukraine.

Furthermore, “Reference was also made to efforts to promote humanitarian initiatives, especially with regard to the release of prisoners.” The Vatican, through the engagement of Cardinal Matteo Zuppi, has been involved in seeking the exchange of prisoners between Russia and Ukraine, and it seems with some success.

The statement concluded by saying that both the pope and the Ukrainian president again expressed the hope that “with the commitment and collaboration of the international community, a cessation of hostilities and a just and lasting peace can be achieved as soon as possible.” Pope Leo has also repeatedly called for an end to this war and for a just and lasting peace achieved through dialogue and negotiations. He has spoken by phone with Russia’s president Vladimir Putin and has publicly offered the Vatican as a venue for peace negotiations, but Russia has rejected this. 

After his conversation with the pope, President Zelensky also issued a statement via Telegram which read:

“I spoke today with Pope Leo XIV. Right during this conversation, Russia attacked Ukraine again – hundreds of Shahed drones and dozens of missiles against our cities and towns. The attack has been ongoing since nightfall, and at least five regions have already been hit. Not a single hour of rest for our people, and this is Russia’s response to our proposal for a ceasefire at Easter. Essentially, the Russians have only increased the intensity of the strikes and, instead of calm in the sky, are carrying out an Easter escalation. This cannot be ignored, and I am grateful to everyone in the world who does not stay silent about this.”

President Zelensky said he “also thanked the Vatican for its role in helping to return our kidnapped children and for all the humanitarian aid it has provided to our people, especially during this hard winter. We also discussed the situation in the Middle East and in the Gulf region.”

From his very first speech as pope on the day of his election, Pope Leo XIV has called for peace and an end to the armed conflict. On Easter Sunday, he will again address the world. and it is expected that he will speak out strongly and call for an end to the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, as well as in other countries around the world.

Robert Rudolph Remus (born August 27, 1948), better known as Sgt. Slaughter, is an American voice actor and retired professional wrestler. He is signed to WWE in its ambassador program.[6]

Second return to the WWF (1990–1994)
Iraqi sympathizer (1990–1991)
In June 1990, Slaughter returned to the WWF as a heel.[23] The August 1990 invasion of Kuwait by Ba'athist Iraq triggered a political crisis that would lead to the 1991 Gulf War, in which Kuwait was freed by a U.S.-led military coalition. A decision was made to have Slaughter support the Iraqi cause, not for the actual political reasons, but more for the fact that Slaughter liked "brutality" and the Iraqi government was "brutal" while the United States regime was said by Slaughter to have become "soft" and "weak". Slaughter aligned himself with an Iraqi enthusiast and kayfabe Iraqi military general, General Adnan (his old rival who left the AWA shortly after Slaughter did).[2][3] They entered a feud with Volkoff, with Slaughter winning the majority of their encounters at house shows.[23] On November 22, at Survivor Series, The Alliance (Volkoff, Tito Santana and The Bushwhackers) defeated The Mercenaries (Slaughter, Boris Zhukov and The Orient Express).[24] As part of his character change, Slaughter began wearing Arab headdresses to the ring, adopted the camel clutch as one of his finishers, and was (kayfabe) photographed meeting with Saddam Hussein. While portraying a turncoat, Slaughter and his family received numerous death threats and he could not go anywhere in public without wearing a bullet-proof vest, having to be surrounded with security personnel at all times.[3][10]By the end of the year, Slaughter set his sights on the WWF Championship, held by Ultimate Warrior. At the Royal Rumble on January 19, 1991, days after the Gulf War air campaign had begun, Slaughter defeated the Warrior to win the WWF Championship after interference from "Macho King" Randy Savage.[2][25] He was immediately challenged by Royal Rumble winner Hulk Hogan, who was furious that Slaughter had (kayfabe) desecrated the American flag (off-screen) as part of his victory celebration. Hogan demanded a match against Slaughter at WrestleMania VII on March 24 in Los Angeles, California, where Slaughter lost the WWF Championship to Hogan.[26] After WrestleMania, Slaughter introduced his newest ally, Colonel Mustafa (his old nemesis The Iron Sheik), teaming with him and Adnan in a three-on-two handicap match against Hogan and Warrior at SummerSlam on August 26, which they lost.[27]

Pope Leo XIV[a] (born Robert Francis Prevost,[b] pronounced /ˈpriːvoʊst/ PREE-vohst;[3][c] September 14, 1955) is the head of the Catholic Church and sovereign of Vatican City.

Born in Chicago, United States, Prevost became a friar in the Order of Saint Augustine in 1977 and was ordained as a priest in 1982. He earned a Doctor of Canon Law degree in 1987 from the Pontifical University of St. Thomas Aquinas in Rome. He performed extensive missionary work in Peru in the 1980s and 1990s, working as a parish pastor, diocesan official, seminary teacher, and administrator. Elected prior general of the Order of Saint Augustine, he was based in Rome from 2001 to 2013, though traveled extensively. He then returned to Peru as Bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023, and became a Peruvian citizen. In 2023, Pope Francis appointed him prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops in Rome, and president of the Pontifical Commission for Latin America. Upon his return to Rome, Prevost was made a cardinal.

AI Overview
These three names share a deep linguistic and historical connection, primarily originating in Ancient Mesopotamia, the Middle East, and the Caucasus.
Sargon
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako
Origin & Etymology: Sako operates on a few different historical tracks depending on the region:
In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.
In the Balkans: In Albania, it functions as a standalone occupational surname for a "church servant" or as a nickname for the Muslim name Isak (Isaac).
In Asia: It is also an unrelated Japanese surname (written as 佐古) meaning "HELP" and "ancient".

California and New York only offer limited or temporary licenses.

How it works: The doctor must already have a medical degree from abroad, pass the U.S. licensing exams, prove they trained or practiced as a doctor for several years in their home country, and get a job offer (often in a rural or underserved area). They then work under supervision for 1–3 years on a temporary license. After that, they can apply for a full, unrestricted license.”

This cartoon pretty much says it all.

Chicago is in a state where law-abiding citizens need government permission just to possess a firearm, and carrying one concealed requires another license, 16 hours of approved training and a $150 application fee. Illinois has built one of the more restrictive gun-control systems in America.

And yet criminals apparently missed the memo.

Over the weekend, Chicago police reported 22 separate shooting incidents. Thirty-eight people were wounded and three were killed, meaning 41 people were shot in roughly 54 hours. One Washington Park shooting alone left one man dead and 14 others wounded.

That is the fundamental problem with pretending gun laws automatically equal public safety. Criminals, by definition, are willing to break laws. Meanwhile, the citizen who actually follows the law has to navigate the rules before having a firearm available when seconds might matter.

President Trump responded by offering federal help.

“Nobody should be forced to live under these conditions,” Trump wrote, adding, “I am awaiting the call,” and directly telling Gov. JB Pritzker, “CALL!!!”

Don’t hold your breath.

Pritzker and Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson responded by blaming Trump, in part, for cuts to federal violence-prevention programs. Johnson pointed to more than $800 million in Justice Department grant cuts nationwide.

There is some important context they leave out. The administration did shift the priorities of a federal community violence intervention grant program, emphasizing law enforcement and immigration enforcement. Chicago then announced it would not even apply for those grants because it objected to the new requirements.

So apparently Washington is supposed to provide money exactly the way Chicago politicians demand, but federal assistance offered on Washington’s terms is unacceptable.

Meanwhile, people keep getting shot.

At some point protecting innocent Chicagoans ought to matter more than protecting the political narrative.

text:
There is $7.93 trillion sitting in money market funds right now while institutional fund managers run cash at 3.5% of assets.

Institutions are nearly fully invested. Private capital is sitting in cash collecting ~4% nominal yield, thinking they have eliminated risk.

They haven't. They have traded visible market volatility for invisible purchasing power destruction.

Look at our historical inflation-adjusted decomposition of $100 since 1950:

• $100 in S&P 500 (Real, After Inflation): $3,241 
• $100 in Cash Under the Mattress (Real Purchasing Power): $7

That is a 460-to-1 terminal divergence.

The macro trap of holding excess cash:

1.) The Yield Illusion: A 4% nominal return feels great until you subtract taxes and real inflation. Your real net return is near zero.

2.) Reinvestment Risk: Cash yields do not lock in duration. The moment the Fed cuts policy rates, those money market yields reset lower overnight.

3.) Liquidity Washouts: Institutional money does not wait for retail cash to feel comfortable. By the time cash moves off the sidelines, the multiple expansion has already happened.

Cash is a tactical tool for liquidity and volatility buffers, not a wealth-compounding vehicle.

Know what you own, understand the cost of sitting out, and let capital compound in real assets.

Sources: 
Investment Company Institute, BofA Global Research, FactSet, Standard & Poor's. Analysis: Momentum Wealth Management.

text:
The most prominent genetic risk factor identified in Blacks is found in the APOL1 gene. Two specific variants of this gene, known as G1 and G2, are found almost exclusively in people of West African descent.

If an individual inherits two copies of these risk variants (one from each parent), their risk of organ damage spikes. Genomic studies, such as data from the VA Million Veteran Program, confirmed that hospitalized COVID-19 patients with the high-risk APOL1 profile faced significantly higher odds of acute kidney injury (AKI), severe glomerular kidney disease, and death.

Sub-Saharan African populations show a natural selection for a specific CCR3 variant (rs17217831-A), which drives higher baseline eosinophil counts and correlates with a causally decreased risk of critical illness.

In summary people of African descent do not have a uniform genetic vulnerability to COVID-19. Instead, they possess a complex genetic landscape: unique variations like APOL1 and MAP3K19 make their kidneys and lungs more susceptible to severe injury during an infection, while variants like OAS1 offer potent antiviral defenses.

When mapping susceptibility specifically within the internally diverse sub-ancestries and isolated groups of Europe, geneticists found that individuals with high Western Hunter-Gatherer (WHG) ancestry and Finns were among the most susceptible to severe COVID-19, while individuals with high Yamnaya-related/Bell Beaker ancestry and Ashkenazi Jews were among the least susceptible.

The Most Susceptible European Populations were High Western Hunter-Gatherer (WHG) Ancestry (Southern Europe), while completely asymptomatic COVID-19 patients possessed discernibly higher proportions of Ancestral North Eurasian (ANE) and Eastern Hunter-Gatherer (EHG) ancestry.

Among Asian populations, broad categorization masks deep regional differences. Genetic mapping and large-scale demographic tracking demonstrate that South Asians (specifically individuals of Bangladeshi and Pakistani descent) were the most biologically vulnerable to severe COVID-19, while East Asians (including Chinese and Japanese populations) were among the least susceptible to severe clinical outcomes.

Interestingly, Bangladesh is also globally recognized as one of the most susceptible countries to climate change. The country consistently ranks among the most climate-vulnerable nations in international assessments. It is among the highest tiers for natural disaster risk.

Bangladesh cames an estimated population of 175 million people packed into an area roughly the size of the U.S. state of Iowa. Because the population density is so extreme, any single cyclone or riverbank erosion event directly impacts millions of lives simultaneously.

text:
African witchcraft for European problems: glycan-mediated intracellular delivery

I jest. Somewhat.

Over the past fortnight, I have acquired an occupational hazard: occasionally, a machine on my desk appears to know which experiment a laboratory ought to perform before the laboratory actually performs it. In Europe, one might dignify this as computational science. Being African, I retain the option of blaming the ancestors.

At the centre of the machine is the Glycan Causal Addressability Engine, or GCAE. It began as a deterministic system for working backwards from therapeutic intent to cellular address. What has emerged since is something broader: a machine that can identify the unresolved causal distinction blocking the next scientific inference and derive the experiment required to force the surviving explanations apart.

The utility of that capability becomes unusually clear in a current research programme at the University of Iowa.

The Iowa misdirection

A laboratory can execute flawless science for years yet fail to answer its core question. Failure usually stems not from poor measurement or execution, but from framing the problem incorrectly: when one experimental control moves two causes at once, or fundamentally different failures masquerade as identical results. Greater precision then merely describes the outcome without revealing its cause.

These are not small boys. George Weiner and his colleagues at the University of Iowa operate at the serious end of American translational cancer research, with institutional depth, modern experimental capability and considerable biological sophistication. That is precisely why Iowa matters. If a causal ambiguity capable of wasting years can survive inside a programme of this calibre, the vulnerability belongs not to one laboratory but to the method by which an industry maps causality.

Imagine a car designed by a lunatic. It has one pedal. Press it gently and the throttle opens. Press further and the throttle opens wider, but the same pedal also begins to apply the brake. The car accelerates, reaches a maximum speed, then slows even as your foot presses harder. No scientist designed this car. Biology did.

The Iowa group is studying vidutolimod (Vidu), a virus-like particle carrying a TLR9 agonist that relies on anti-Qβ capsid antibodies for uptake and activation in plasmacytoid dendritic cells. However, antibody-coated Vidu also engages BDCA2: while this aids entry, stronger engagement and internalisation suppress the intended type I interferon response.

In this analogy, anti-Qβ coating acts as the pedal, productive Vidu/TLR9 cargo delivery as the throttle, BDCA2 inhibitory signalling as the brake, and the interferon response as the car's speed.

Experiments demonstrate a Goldilocks effect: low anti-Qβ yields weak uptake, intermediate levels produce a peak interferon response, and high levels increase BDCA2 internalisation while reducing interferon output. An orthogonal experiment using a soluble TLR9 agonist with increasing BDCA2 engagement confirmed this inhibition independently of Vidu delivery, proving the 'brake' exists.

The paper reports that the group is now examining machinery downstream of BDCA2—including Syk recruitment and phosphorylation, calcium mobilisation and IRF7 nuclear translocation—to understand the inhibitory pathway more deeply. That is scientifically reasonable. But a prior causal obligation remains. In the actual Vidu system, the same experimental control still appears capable of changing both throttle and brake. Mapping the brake more beautifully cannot, by itself, tell us how much of a change in vehicle speed came from braking and how much from altered acceleration.

This is the split GCAE catches IMMEDIATELY. It does not permit BDCA2 internalisation to stand as a single explanatory variable because the anti-Qβ sweep simultaneously changes two consequence-bearing states: the productive Vidu/TLR9 cargo state and the inhibitory BDCA2 receptor state. The observed interferon response is downstream of both. Until those two causal contributions can be separated, the machine withholds the stronger attribution: the experiment has reached an evidential frontier, and the next scientific obligation is to obtain an observation or intervention capable of distinguishing the two branches.

A downstream computation turns that obligation into an almost embarrassingly economical experiment. Vary the anti-Qβ coating, but also vary the Vidu particle dose. Traverse both controls across a small nine-condition grid and ask whether they genuinely move the biology in two independent directions. In the car, the objective is to find two classes of comparison: one in which acceleration is held approximately constant while braking changes, and another in which braking is held approximately constant while acceleration changes.

That is what the system has done without the laboratory first performing the experiment.

The complete Iowa computation is attached below for technical scrutiny.

The biological hospital

Glycans are sugar structures that biological systems can read. Cells carry molecular readers on their surfaces, and particular glycan structures can sometimes be exploited as addresses, helping guide a therapeutic construct towards a chosen cell.

The original problem was cellular addressability. Given a target cell, payload, intracellular destination and required biological consequence, GCAE searches its evidence-bound scientific state for routes consistent with that mission. The machinery beneath this, the Polyoptic Parallax Engine, or P², took years to develop. GCAE did not. It emerged in its present form in less than a fortnight to test a narrower proposition: could a causal machine identify a plausible cellular address while preserving exactly where the evidence ended and what still had to be established before that address could responsibly be acted upon?

Almost immediately, the lesser half of the problem became obvious. Finding the address is not the same thing as delivering the payload.

Imagine the body as a vast hospital. Somewhere inside is the ward you need. Inside that ward is a particular room. Inside that room is the biological machinery your treatment must ultimately influence. The medicine is an aerosol sealed inside a specialised canister and packed into a parcel. For treatment to succeed, the parcel must survive the journey to the hospital, enter through the intended route, reach the correct ward, survive the hospital's internal sorting system, arrive at the correct room, cross any final secured boundary, open, and release enough active medicine in a form the patient can actually use.

The difficulty is that you cannot walk freely through this hospital and watch every handover. You remain largely outside, receiving fragments of evidence: a security log confirming that the parcel entered; an occasional camera image placing it somewhere inside; a chemical trace recovered from a corridor; perhaps a record that it reached the correct floor; and, eventually, some indication of whether the patient improved. Between those observations lies an invisible chain of custody.

The parcel may be damaged before arrival, quarantined by security, misrouted by the receiving desk, returned to the entrance or destroyed as waste. It may reach the correct ward but never leave the receiving room. The canister may arrive intact but refuse to open, open in the corridor, or open correctly only to reveal that the active ingredient has degraded. From outside, every failure can produce the same report: the patient did not improve. Inside the causal system, they are different events and demand different remedies.

The biological correspondence is direct. The journey to the hospital is manufacture, administration and biological exposure. The target cell is the ward. Receptor recognition and cellular entry are the controlled entrance. Intracellular trafficking is the internal routing system. The relevant compartment is the room. A membrane that must still be crossed is the secured door. Cargo release is the canister opening. Formation of the active biological species is the aerosol becoming respirable. Only then can the patient respond.

This is why improving a construct before localising its failure can be actively misleading. If security confiscates the parcel, redesigning the canister's release valve is pointless. If the mailroom routes every package to the incinerator, a faster courier merely feeds the fire faster. If the parcel reaches the correct room but the canister never opens, improving the ward address solves the wrong problem. Yet all three interventions can sound sensible when the only diagnosis available is 'delivery failure'.

Because we cannot simply enter the biological hospital and inspect every transfer of custody, the first plausible explanation can harden into the programme's organising assumption. More parcels are sent. The label is redesigned. The courier is accelerated. The canister is rebuilt. All while the original package sits in quarantine. The first useful question is therefore not how to improve the construct, but: Where, exactly, did the productive route cease to exist?

That question changed the machine. GCAE first learnt to find the correct ward. It then had to reason about the parcel's hidden journey through the building—not by pretending every internal event could be observed directly, but by asking which observations, taken at which checkpoints, would force competing hidden routes to produce different evidence.

The machine traces the molecular population actually manufactured and administered through biological exposure, cellular encounter, receptor engagement, internalisation, sorting, retention, degradation, membrane crossing, cargo release, active-species formation and ultimate biological effect. At each transfer of custody, it preserves the competing futures still compatible with the evidence. A delay is not a diversion. A diversion is not destruction. A parcel merely seen inside the building is not a parcel delivered intact to the correct room. And the presence of cargo is not proof that the cargo remains capable of doing its job.

The machine is equally strict about what counts as delivery. Fluorescent brightness does not get to impersonate productive transport. A camera image showing the parcel somewhere inside the hospital does not establish that it reached the correct room, remained intact, crossed the necessary boundary or opened there. A bright signal may represent material attached to the cell surface, degraded material, material trapped in the wrong compartment, or intact cargo travelling productively. Those states can look similar while being causally opposite.

What an unknown becomes

Once those distinctions are preserved, uncertainty changes character. An unknown no longer means merely 'we do not know'. It becomes: This is what we do not know. This is the conclusion it prevents us from drawing. These are the explanations still compatible with the evidence. This observation would force them apart. And these are the deductions each possible answer would permit or destroy.

No biological fact has changed. No new measurement has appeared, and an unknown has not become known through rhetorical force. What has changed is the structure surrounding the unknown. The machine identifies which unresolved proposition blocks the next inference, derives the experiment that forces surviving explanations to disagree, states what each possible result would eliminate or preserve, and specifies where computation may resume. The next experiment is selected not merely because its result would be interesting, but because the unresolved causal structure makes it necessary.

Iowa is the concrete instance. The facts were already present; GCAE changed the structure surrounding what remained unresolved. It identified the entanglement as the blocking defect and mandated separation of the productive-cargo and receptor-state branches. A downstream computation then compiled that obligation into the minimum experiment required to determine whether the existing system could separate them.

A causal experiment compiler

That is the broader capability which has emerged most clearly over the past fortnight. With GCAE at its centre, the system is becoming not merely an addressability engine or a machine for localising causal failure, but a causal experiment compiler.

Many systems can suggest experiments. A language model can generate plausible hypotheses. A literature engine can recommend relevant papers. An optimiser can rank candidate molecules. This system attempts something stricter. GCAE establishes the scientific state, preserves the surviving causal alternatives, identifies the earliest unresolved distinction blocking a stronger conclusion, and specifies the evidential obligation required to separate them. Downstream computation can then compile that obligation into an experiment, determine what each possible result would permit, invalidate or leave unresolved, and establish where computation may lawfully resume.

The experiment is not appended to the analysis as a sensible recommendation. It is compiled from the unresolved causal structure.

The same ward, a different room

Changing the payload highlights this distinction. GCAE also evaluates BDCA2-mediated siRNA delivery to plasmacytoid dendritic cells; the same hospital and ward, but a different target room.

While Vidu's TLR9 agonist functions within the endosomal system, siRNA must cross an additional membrane into the cytosol. Thus, a route successful for Vidu can leave siRNA stranded. Delivery requires reaching the specific site of action, not merely entering the cell.

Accordingly, GCAE orders its evaluations causally: initial construct state in blood, BDCA2 engagement, post-internalisation trafficking, cytosolic entry, and off-target or safety effects. Downstream experiments rely on preceding results; perfecting later steps is useless if early transport fails.

GCAE has evolved to map routes, locate failed handovers, and derive the observation required to reveal why they failed in a partially observable biological interior.

Assays offer limited glimpses, but causal computation establishes precisely what each observation proves.

The cost of the wrong failure

Without pinpointing a failed handover, increasing throughput only accelerates the wrong process and risks optimising failure.

The system accelerates science by computing dependency structures before committing capital. GCAE identifies the specific stage requiring investment, from manufacture to biological action, and localises the critical uncertainty; downstream computation compiles the necessary experiment, ensuring downstream work relies only on proven upstream assumptions.

Nature provides answers, but GCAE decides which questions to ask and in what order.

Conducting logically necessary experiments rather than merely interesting ones saves more than money.

It is time; the one reagent science has never learned how to manufacture.

Perhaps the ancestors are whispering after all.

🏈 JAKE NAWROT: A FUTURE FACE OF KENTUCKY FOOTBALL? 🔵⚪

@JakeNawrot's road to becoming one of the nation’s elite quarterbacks wasn’t built on early hype. Growing up in Illinois, Nawrot developed into a two-sport athlete at John Hersey High School in Arlington Heights, playing both football and basketball. Football also runs in the family — his father, Paul Nawrot, played at Iowa in the 1990s.

Jake had to wait for his opportunity. As a sophomore, he sat behind future UCLA quarterback Colton Gumino and saw very limited varsity action. But when Nawrot finally became Hersey’s starter as a junior, he exploded onto the national recruiting scene. He threw for 3,078 yards and 41 touchdowns with only two interceptions, completing roughly 71% of his passes while helping Hersey reach the Illinois Class 7A state quarterfinals.

Suddenly, the kid who had spent much of his early high school career waiting his turn was one of the most coveted quarterbacks in America. Nawrot earned an invitation to the prestigious Elite 11 Finals and developed into a top-five national quarterback prospect, drawing comparisons to NFL quarterback Drake Maye for his combination of size, arm talent, accuracy and instincts.

Then came the decision that could help shape the future of Kentucky football. On April 12, 2026, Nawrot committed to Will Stein and the Kentucky Wildcats, choosing UK over programs including Oregon, Iowa and Kansas State.

For Stein, Nawrot could become much more than another recruit. He has the talent to become the centerpiece of Kentucky’s offense and one of the faces of the new era in Lexington. With Stein’s history developing quarterbacks and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan’s experience working with elite talent, Kentucky offers Nawrot an opportunity to develop while competing in the SEC.

He still has his senior season of high school ahead of him, and nothing will be handed to him when he arrives in Lexington. But the potential is enormous.

From waiting his turn at Hersey to becoming an elite national quarterback prospect — Jake Nawrot could be the quarterback who helps define the Will Stein era at Kentucky.

🔵⚪ The future of Kentucky Football is looking bright.

text:
Grok:  Proof of citizenship isn’t a poll tax. The 24th Amendment banned taxes as a condition of voting. Incidental costs of documents most Americans already have (or can get free/low-cost alternatives for) are not that. The Supreme Court rejected the “poll tax” framing for voter ID in Crawford v. Marion County (2008). States that require ID typically offer free photo IDs; birth certificates and similar records are used for jobs, licenses, benefits, and travel—not invented as a voting barrier.
Requiring eligible citizens to confirm they are eligible citizens is ordinary list maintenance. Treating it as Jim Crow is rhetorical, not legal.

Confirmed problems since 2015 are not theoretical:
Heritage’s database now catalogs well over 1,500 proven cases (convictions, official findings, judicial findings) covering false registrations, double voting, absentee/ballot-harvesting fraud, ineligible voting, and related offenses. It is a sampling, not a complete census—many cases are never investigated.

Audits and official reviews keep finding non-citizens on the rolls and, in smaller numbers, ballots cast. Examples include Georgia’s review (dozens of confirmed non-citizens among millions of records), Iowa (hundreds registered, dozens who voted after SAVE checks), New Jersey’s 2026 software-error admission (~6,600 non-citizens registered, ~400 who voted), Virginia analyses of self-declared non-citizens who voted before removal, plus smaller confirmed clusters in Florida, Alabama, Ohio, Montana, and elsewhere. Federal prosecutions under the 1996 alien-voting statute exist; they are not zero.

Multi-state and deceased registrants: Public Interest Legal Foundation and similar reviews have repeatedly documented hundreds of thousands of deceased names still on rolls and thousands of people appearing to vote in more than one state in a given cycle.

Documented localized schemes: 2018 North Carolina 9th District (ballot harvesting that forced a new election), Bridgeport, CT 2023 Democratic primary (ballot stuffing; new primary ordered), plus repeated absentee and registration-fraud convictions in multiple states.

Michigan is not an exception. Clerks have raised citizenship and QVF concerns; Benson’s office has faced lawsuits over list maintenance, record retention, and access; the Board of Canvassers deadlocked 2–2 and kept a citizenship-proof petition off the ballot after a long delay despite hundreds of thousands of signatures. Polling cited in coverage of that fight showed large majorities of Michigan voters (including many Democrats) favor citizens-only voting and proof of citizenship. Blocking that measure is not “protecting access.” It is protecting the status quo on rolls.

Fraud does not have to flip a presidential election to matter. Inaccurate rolls, unprosecuted illegal registrations, and weak chain-of-custody on mail ballots dilute legal votes. Countries with high-integrity elections require ID and citizenship documentation without calling it a poll tax. The people most harmed by sloppy rolls are the citizens whose votes are supposed to count equally.

text:
Per @tloving138 Bowling Green–Warren County Drug Task Force Dismantles Illegal Marijuana Vape Manufacturing Operation
The Bowling Green–Warren County Drug Task Force, with assistance from the Kentucky State Police Interdiction Team, arrested four individuals following an eight-week investigation into an illegal marijuana vape manufacturing operation being conducted in unsanitary and non-sterile conditions inside a residential garage yesterday, September 1, 2026
Arrested:
•Javon E. Mitchell, 24, of 1250 Peachtree Lane, Bowling Green, KY
•Dayshawn M. Mitchell, 27, of 1407 Calgary Way, Bowling Green, KY
•Savyon O. Howard, 24, of 614 Kirtley Way, Bowling Green, KY
•George D. Murray, 56, of 1309 Scottsville Road, Bowling Green, KY
All four individuals were charged with:
1Trafficking in Marijuana, over 5 pounds, Class C Felony — Gun Enhancement
2Engaging in Organized Crime
Following an eight-week investigation and surveillance operation, detectives established probable cause to obtain a search warrant for a residence located at 1407 Calgary Way in northern Warren County.
When detectives arrived to execute the search warrant, the occupants refused to open the door, and officers made a forcible entry into the residence. Once the residence was secured, the occupants offered no resistance and were taken into custody.
During the search, detectives discovered a clandestine marijuana vape manufacturing operation being conducted inside the garage. Investigators located marijuana vape products and evidence

indicating that the products were being manufactured and processed in unsanitary, non-sterile conditions not suitable for the production of a consumer product.
This is the first marijuana vape manufacturing operation of this type encountered by the Bowling Green - Warren County Drug Task Force in it’s 29 year history.
Investigators are particularly concerned about the potential impact of illegally manufactured marijuana vape products on high school students and young adults, who are frequently targeted by illicit vape and marijuana product distribution.
This investigation highlights the dangers associated with illegal drug manufacturing operations being conducted inside residential properties. “These products are manufactured outside of any legitimate regulatory or safety standards, creating additional risks for the individuals who ultimately consume them.”
All accused were lodged in the Warren County Regional Jail.
During the execution of the search warrant, Detectives and Troopers located and seized 2,146 illegally manufactured marijuana vape products, hundreds of commercial appearing packaging boxes for the vapes, more than two gallons of liquid marijuana extract, which investigators estimate to be the equivalent of approximately 10 pounds of marijuana, 48 oxycodone tablets, two handguns, one shotgun, and $3,489 in cash. A 2015 Jeep Grand Cherokee was also seized in connection with the investigation.
The investigation remains ongoing, and additional charges are possible.

SPRINGDALE, Ark. [August 31, 2026] – 7 Brew®, the fastest growing beverage brand in the country known for its high-energy experience and more than 20,000 customizable drink combinations, is teaming up with LSU Athletics and giving Tiger fans another reason to cheer this football season with a chance to win 7 Brew all season long. 
 
As an Official Partner of LSU, 7 Brew is introducing “Sips for Kicks,” a special promotion tied to every regular season game. How it works is if the LSU kickers score seven or more points in a game, Tiger fans will unlock a buy one, get one free 7 Brew offer on all drinks at participating locations. Fans can take part in the promotion immediately following the game and through the close of business the following day. 
 
“LSU fans bring incredible energy every Saturday, and we wanted to create something that lets us celebrate right along with them,” said Nick Chavez, Chief Marketing Officer. To celebrate the start of football season and the new multi-year partnership, LSU fans can score exclusive rewards and giveaways all season long, starting with the School Pennant Giveaway on Sept. 4. Guests who buy any two medium or large drinks get a free LSU x 7 Brew pennant, the perfect gameday accessory, while supplies last. 
 
“LSU fans are among the most passionate in college sports, and we’re always looking for partners who can add to the excitement of being a Tiger,” said Ben Price, General Manager, LSU. “7 Brew brings a fun, high-energy approach to this partnership, and ‘Sips for Kicks’ gives our fans another reason to celebrate every point on Saturdays. We’re excited to welcome 7 Brew to the LSU family and bring this partnership to life throughout the season.”

text:
County Secures $150,000 to Advance Economic Growth in Southern Worcester

Worcester County Tourism and Economic Development (WCTED), in partnership with the Tri-County Council for the Lower Eastern Shore (TCC) is launching a comprehensive economic development project to identify opportunities for industry growth, private investment, and job creation in southern Worcester County.

This initiative, entitled Opportunities for Economic Growth and Industry Diversification in Worcester County, Maryland, will be funded by a $75,000 grant from the U.S. Economic Development Administration (EDA) and a $75,000 match from the TCC. The study will outline practical steps to improve essential infrastructure, prepare workers for new job opportunities, attract and support businesses, and expand the types of industries operating in Worcester County. These efforts will help create a stronger, more resilient economy in Worcester County and across the Lower Eastern Shore.

“Southern Worcester County has tremendous assets and opportunities that we can build on,” Commissioner Caryn Abbott said. “This funding will allow us to take a close look at what businesses need to grow and thrive, where new opportunities exist, and what investments can be made now and going forward to convert that potential into good jobs and ongoing economic growth for our communities.”

The study will explore ways to expand manufacturing, aerospace, defense, and technology industries, particularly in Pocomoke City. Pocomoke offers several advantages for business growth, including the 175-acre Pocomoke Industrial Park, access to U.S. Routes 13 and 113, freight rail service, natural gas, and Pocomoke River access. Pocomoke has also secured Enterprise Zone, HUBZone, and Opportunity Zone designations, which provide tax benefits, investment incentives, and access to certain federal contracting opportunities that can help existing businesses grow and encourage new employers to locate there. Pocomoke’s proximity to NASA’s Wallops Flight Facility creates further opportunities to attract companies that supply or support the region’s growing aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, and technology industries.

To build on these advantages, the study will determine whether local water and wastewater systems, electricity, broadband, roads, rail service, river access, and industrial sites can support new and expanding businesses, like Hardwire, while also identifying opportunities to attract suppliers supporting NASA Wallops Flight Facility, Rocket Lab, and other regional employers. It will also identify needed improvements, examine the types of workers employers are seeking, and recommend ways to prepare local residents for specialized, well-paying jobs.

“The resulting roadmap will identify infrastructure investments, workforce development needs, business recruitment opportunities, and implementation steps to strengthen the local economy and position southern Worcester County for future investment,” WCTED Director Melanie Pursel said.

Recent growth at Pocomoke-based Hardwire, LLC, which secured a $99 million contract award, provides a timely example of the economic potential already taking shape in southern Worcester County.

“The time is right for a comprehensive look at Pocomoke City,” TCC Executive Director Greg Padgham said. “Its unique geographical location combined with existing and planned assets and infrastructure make Pocomoke City an up-and-coming hub for the Lower Eastern Shore. This contributes to the region’s economic diversification and resiliency and is one of the reasons the Tri-County Council and its partners in the Philadelphia office of EDA were happy to fund the study.”

Ultimately, the initiative will provide Worcester County and its partners with a data-driven strategy to expand manufacturing, attract private investment, create quality year-round jobs, strengthen the commercial tax base, and position southern Worcester County as a regional center for innovation and technology-driven economic growth.

The Maryland Department of Natural Resources will open the archery hunting season for white-tailed and sika deer on Sept. 11. The season runs through Jan. 31, 2027 with several breaks for muzzleloader and firearms season. 

In addition, the seventh annual Primitive Deer Hunt Days from Feb. 1-3, 2027 offer archers using vertical longbows and vertical recurve bows a few more days afield.

Multiple Sundays are open to archery hunting in most counties, including on some public lands. Hunters should consult the 2026-2027 Maryland Guide to Hunting and Trapping for additional information on specific dates and closures in their region. Read more:
