text:
Parents should find a way to have their children attend college without taking out student loans. 

That means if your child doesn’t get substantive merit scholarships to out of state and big name schools, they attend the in-state school. Employers look past the name of the school. It’s not what they are looking at. 

Don’t take out big loans for school. If your child is 4.0 gpa + SAT exceeding 1400, they will get some merit offers that you can consider for out of state, otherwise NO. 

You can fund a school year through the payment plan so you won’t need to pay it all upfront each semester. 

Still can’t avoid a loan? Start the first year at community college. 

Employers care that you graduated from a 4 year institution (if the job requires it), they don’t care where you started. Your degree will be from Florida State, or West Chester University, or University of South Carolina, etc. Community College can be one of the best hacks in education - and I can tell you from taking continuing courses throughout my entire career (not for a degree) that the professors can be every bit as serious and good as a 4 year institution. Not always but in many cases, and your child is likely taking general education classes to get started. 

The Educational Loan Industrial Complex has fueled the decline in four year institutions across this great nation. How you ask? They drove the explosion in administrative position growth at every college. Administrative positions have one purpose (with exceptions) and that is to create friction that students must overcome to getting their degree.

text:
Not the Prettiest Start, but a Beautiful Finish: Kaden Howard’s Journey from a 2–18 Program to Power Four Georgia Tech

While many players entered ninth grade chasing powerhouse programs, Kaden Howard stayed at Palm Glades Prep. His team went 2–18 during his first two years of high school—probably one of the worst records in South Florida—but I told him, “Stay, build your film, and I’ll do the rest.” He listened every step of the way.

Kaden had the size and production, and his verified 40-yard dash proved he had legitimate speed—not just success against the competition. Even with multiple offers entering his senior year, I explained that college coaches still wanted an official 100-meter time. Without hesitation, he joined the track team at Keys Gate Charter, ran faster than I expected, and his video went viral with nearly 50.8 million views on @Jerry_RisingStars. Keys Gate Charter and its track program deserve tremendous credit for giving him the opportunity to showcase his speed.

While playing at an unknown school with one of South Florida’s worst records, Kaden earned 10 FBS offers—including an SEC offer from Mississippi State. Think about that: He received an offer from a program in the best conference in college football while playing at a school many people had never heard of and for a team that had won only two games.

After transferring to Miami Palmetto, he became the highest-rated Class of 2027 wide receiver in Miami-Dade County and committed to Power Four Georgia Tech.

Academically, Kaden entered his senior year with all high school graduation requirements completed and a 3.66 GPA. He has been a student at Rise Preparatory Academy since his sophomore year.

Hopefully, another young athlete learns from Kaden’s journey: You don’t have to attend the biggest-name school to reach the highest level. Get the film, be productive, prove your measurables, handle your academics, listen—and most importantly, find knowledgeable people with real college connections who can guide you.

Sometimes, the right guidance matters more than the school name.

text:
the (avengers) endgame of rank and rent is owning 6 spots in every search result in your city, and all the leads funnel back to you. 

become the thanos of rank and rent.

here's the full network structure from this week:

the setup is a pyramid. your main rank and rent (houston cleaning services) has a page for every sub-service. then each big sub-service ALSO gets its own dedicated rank and rent: houston airbnb cleaning, houston move-in cleaning, houston move-out cleaning. now you have two properties competing for the same keyword, your service page and the standalone EMD site. whichever one they click, the lead routes to you. that's how you go from ranking for searches to owning them.

the reason this works right now is an arbitrage window. people search in chatgpt-length sentences now, "team of four for a spring cleaning of a 2,000 square foot house in houston heights." old rank and rents were one page targeting one keyword. these multi-page builds catch every long tail variation, and with AI you can one-shot the pages. EMDs plus citations plus tier twos does the rest. tristan said the quiet part: he hopes not too many people start doing this.

then you stack the suburbs. katy is 20 minutes outside houston, so the whole pyramid repeats: katy cleaning services as the hub, sub-service pages on it, then dedicated sub-service rank and rents for katy too. eight sites became the houston core, and the suburbs compound it from there. maximum coverage of a niche within a city. works best in tier one and tier two cities, weaker in small towns where there's nothing to expand into.

the build workflow has no magic prompt. tristan literally talks into his mic for ten minutes: "list every core service a concrete contractor gets called for, turn each into a sub-service rank and rent, list every reason someone searches each one, reverse engineer those into pages." codex lists it, the website builder builds it, and then the one part he refuses to automate: manually reviewing every site before launch. noindex tags, internal links pointing the right way, canonicals. one of the network sites went out noindexed. a second pair of eyes still beats a one shot.

real talk on costs: one site is cheap, fifteen sites is a real monthly nut. domain renewals, callrail, citations for every property. the model still works the same way though, land one partner per site and you're profitable almost immediately on pay per lead. the leads aren't the hard part anymore. the partners are the constraint.
and an offer got born live on the pod: free SEO retainers, the kind tristan charges $5K a month for, for local rank academy members. two conditions, you're a member and you're okay with your business becoming a public case study on youtube. deadline is end of month or until seats fill. backlinks, browser blasts, structure reviews, the same treatment the vet clinic got. ten public case studies running in the background is the plan. jacky's summary of local SEO after watching two businesses rip in real time: "if you can't do it, I swear something's wrong with you guys."

text:
Four years ago, Danny Ellerd weighed 92 pounds, was living under a bridge, and had spent 15 years chained to an addiction that was slowly killing him.

When police found him, this was bigger than another arrest. They were looking at a man whose body had been pushed so far that he was dangerously close to dying.

Danny survived the hospital, but survival only gave him another morning. What happened next required something nobody else could choose for him: he decided his life could not continue this way.

He went to rehab, accepted the help in front of him, put his head down, and began doing the slow, uncomfortable work of rebuilding a life he had spent years tearing apart.

Four years later, that same man graduated from Oklahoma State University with straight A’s and a degree in technology.

This man was on a completely different path.

Brother, people can reach down and help pull you off the pavement. They can open doors, drive you to treatment, forgive you, encourage you, pray for you, and give you another chance when you have already burned through several.

But sooner or later, your feet still have to move.

Your past may explain the scars you carry and the road that brought you here, but it does not get permanent authority over the man you become.

There comes a point when a man has to stop asking what happened to him and start deciding what he is going to do with the life still sitting in front of him.

Danny’s story is important because it shows what can happen when a man finally accepts the hand being offered, stands up, and begins fighting for a future he once could not imagine having.

text:
ATP US Open

Arthur Fery vs Lorenzo Musetti

🧠 Form & Context

Arthur Fery

🔥 The wider form profile is excellent: Fery is 7-3 over his last ten completed matches and 46-21 over the last 52 weeks, a 68.7% win rate. His raw 66.2 CFS is higher than Musetti's.

🟦 His hard-court record is genuinely strong: Fery is 6-5 at ATP level and 15-7 at Challenger/ITF level on hard over the last 52 weeks. Four of his five lower-level titles have come on hard.

🚀 Winston-Salem supplied same-surface rhythm: He reached the final after a deep week of competitive hard-court tennis, proving that his ranking rise is supported by current results rather than only older lower-level volume.

🚨 The final created a fresh-collapse flag: Fery lost 6-3, 6-2 to Ignacio Buse on 29 August and offered limited resistance in the second set. That does not erase the run, but it blocks a positive model adjustment in his favour under the review rules.

🥵 The schedule is the largest risk: Five matches in five days in Winston-Salem, followed by only three days before a humid Grand Slam best-of-five opener, creates a substantial fatigue problem.

🔄 His return profile can still test Musetti: The supplied data show Fery winning roughly 33% of first-serve return points, 52% on second-serve returns and 28% of return games. If physically fresh, he can apply real scoreboard pressure.

Lorenzo Musetti

⚖️ His recent form is solid without being dominant: Musetti is 6-4 in his last ten and 35-20 over the last 52 weeks. His 60.9 CFS trails Fery by 5.3 points but remains Medium-High.

🟦 His hard-court level is proven: Musetti is 29-16 on ATP hard over the last 52 weeks and 91-78 across his ATP hard career. The current surface record is far stronger than the outdated idea that he is only a clay threat.

🧩 The latest defeat was competitive: He lost 7-6, 7-5 to Tiafoe in Cincinnati, a tight result that does not trigger a collapse flag.

🛌 He owns a major rest advantage: Musetti last played on 22 August, giving him roughly ten days to recover and prepare. Fery arrives directly from a physically expensive final run.

🏟️ The class difference remains meaningful: Musetti is ranked No. 14, has reached a career-high No. 5 and owns two ATP titles. Fery's rise is impressive, but his experience at this level is far more limited.

🧠 His second-serve and return balance suits a long match: The supplied profile gives Musetti an 84% service-game hold rate, strong second-serve production and approximately 24.5% of return games won. Those numbers offer several ways to apply pressure if Fery's legs fade.

🔍 Match Breakdown

Raw form makes this look like a possible underdog opportunity. Fery leads CFS, owns an excellent last-52-week record and has just reached a tour final. The problem is timing. That final came after five matches in five days, ended in a 6-3, 6-2 defeat and left only a three-day turnaround before a humid best-of-five opener against a rested Top 15 opponent.

Fery's best route is to start fast. His return numbers are strong enough to challenge Musetti, and he cannot afford to allow the favourite to settle into a long, varied match. Shortening points without abandoning his return aggression is difficult, but it may be necessary because a fourth or fifth set would strongly magnify the recovery gap.

Musetti should be patient. He does not need to attack every early opening or prove the ranking difference immediately. By using height, spin and pace variation, protecting his own second serve and making Fery play repeated physical points, he can allow the scheduling advantage to grow naturally. The biggest risk is a slow start that gives the underdog an early lead and fresh confidence.

A rain interruption would materially help Fery because it could split the physical workload and provide recovery. In uninterrupted humid conditions, the longer format increasingly favours Musetti.

🔮 Prediction

Musetti is the preferred winner, but this is a reduced-confidence call rather than a dismissal of Fery. Fery's underlying form is real and his return profile can make the early stages difficult. Musetti's decisive advantages are class, proven ATP hard-court strength and a much better recovery window.

ATP US Open 

Camilo Ugo Carabelli vs Jan-Lennard Struff

🧠 Form & Context

Camilo Ugo Carabelli

📉 The surface profile is a major limitation: Ugo Carabelli is 7-20 across his ATP hard-court career and 4-13 on ATP hard over the last 52 weeks. His career ATP clay win rate is 50.8%, compared with only 25.9% on hard.

🟫 His résumé is overwhelmingly clay-based: All 13 of his Challenger/ITF titles came on clay. That does not make him incapable on hard, but it explains why his overall ranking can overstate his surface suitability here.

⚖️ Recent form is weak: After result-status exclusions, he is 4-6 in his last ten, 3-7 in his last ten hard matches and 23-27 over the last 52 weeks. His 38.0 CFS is Medium-Low.

✅ His latest completed hard match was a win: He beat Mejia 7-5, 6-4 in Cancun. It was competitive rather than dominant, but it avoids a fresh-collapse flag.

🩺 The next appearance ended in retirement: One day later, he retired against Echargui while trailing 6-2, 5-0. That is treated as a fitness concern—not as a completed loss or evidence about a finished performance.

🧱 The level record is difficult: Ugo Carabelli is 2-10 against Top 50 opponents and 13-23 against the Top 100 over the last 52 weeks.

Jan-Lennard Struff

⚠️ His own hard-court trend is poor: Struff is 4-11 on ATP hard over the last 52 weeks and 2-8 across his last ten hard matches. The favourite is not entering with a strong surface-form cushion.

⚖️ The overall trend is only marginally better: After excluding non-comparable team-league and retirement-decided results, he is 5-5 in his last ten and 27-29 over the last 52 weeks. His 39.1 CFS leads by just 1.1 points.

💥 The serve is the clearest matchup advantage: Struff averages 9.5 aces per match over the last 52 weeks and wins approximately 75% of first-serve points in the supplied profile. Ugo Carabelli averages 3.2 aces and owns much weaker hard-court service protection.

🏟️ The class and big-match résumé remain valuable: Struff beat Medvedev in straight sets and Nakashima in five at Wimbledon. Those were grass results, so they are not direct hard-court proof, but they demonstrate the best-of-five ceiling that Ugo Carabelli has not shown.

📉 The latest hard result was not encouraging: Struff lost 6-3, 6-4 to Tabilo in Cincinnati. It was a moderate straight-sets defeat, not a collapse.

❓ There is no prior meeting: The matchup must be assessed from serve, surface and physical context rather than H2H.

🔍 Match Breakdown

This is not a strong-favourite-versus-strong-underdog form comparison. Both profiles are below the preferred form threshold, and only 1.1 CFS points separate them. Struff's case rests on matchup structure, class and the opponent's surface/fitness problems rather than on a hot recent run.

Struff's first serve should be the single biggest weapon on the court. If he produces his normal ace rate and wins first-serve points near the supplied 75% level, he can keep Ugo Carabelli away from the return exchanges where the Argentine would prefer to build rhythm. The concern is Struff's recent 2-8 hard line: if the first serve drops, his current baseline confidence may not be sufficient to create a comfortable separation.

Ugo Carabelli's route is to extend rallies, make Struff move repeatedly and turn the match into a physical test. At 36, Struff would prefer not to play a long humid match full of repeated defensive sequences. Yet the underdog must first demonstrate that the Cancun retirement has no remaining physical relevance, and his 25.9% career ATP-hard win rate offers little surface reassurance.

Rain could help either side. It may give Ugo Carabelli recovery time if fitness becomes an issue, or allow Struff to repeatedly restart with a fresh serving arm. Because the underlying form gap is so thin, any interruption further reduces confidence.

🔮 Prediction

Struff is the tentative winner pick. His serve, ranking, best-of-five experience and Ugo Carabelli's hard-court/fitness concerns are sufficient to support the favourite, but the recent form numbers are too weak for a normal stake.

ATP US Open 

Francisco Comesana vs Flavio Cobolli

🧠 Form & Context

Francisco Comesana

📉 The current trend is below the level required for this matchup: Comesana is 4-6 in his last ten overall, 3-7 in his last ten on hard and 20-27 over the last 52 weeks. His 37.2 CFS is firmly in the Medium-Low range.

🟦 Hard court remains the weaker side of the profile: His supplied last-52-week hard record is 5-10 across levels, including 5-9 at ATP level. The overall record is not being dragged down by one bad tournament; the surface trend has been persistently difficult.

⚠️ The latest match exposed an uneven level: Comesana lost to Altmaier in Winston-Salem after a 1-6 opening set, although he recovered enough to make the second set a tiebreak. That response was better than a complete collapse, but the slow start is dangerous against a Top 10 opponent.

🎾 He does possess enough serve to stay competitive in phases: Comesana has averaged 6.5 aces per match across the supplied last-52-week sample. He must use that first strike to avoid being placed under immediate scoreboard pressure.

🧱 The opposition-quality record is a major obstacle: He is 0-3 against Top 10 players, 1-4 against the Top 20 and 2-10 against the Top 50 over the last 52 weeks.

🔁 The H2H does not offer a hidden positive: Cobolli won their only meeting 7-5, 2-6, 6-3 in Monte Carlo in April 2026. The clay surface limits its direct relevance here, but it still shows that Comesana did not hold a matchup advantage even in more familiar conditions.

Flavio Cobolli

🚀 Arrives from a Cincinnati semifinal: Cobolli won four matches in that run and lost to Fils in a competitive semifinal. That is the strongest recent tournament performance on either side.

🔥 His hard-court trend is clear: He is 7-3 across his last ten hard matches, 6-4 overall in his last ten and 38-24 across the last 52 weeks. His 63.8 CFS leads Comesana by 26.6 points.

🏆 The class profile has moved to another tier: Cobolli is ranked No. 6, has won three ATP titles and has a positive 58.3% record against Top 20 opponents over the last 52 weeks.

💥 The serve has developed into a larger weapon: His last-52-week ace average is 6.3 per match, up from a 4.4 career average. That improvement matters against an opponent whose best route is to keep service games short.

🟦 He is no longer surface-dependent: Cobolli is 17-15 on ATP hard over the last 52 weeks and owns a career ATP hard record above 50%. The Cincinnati run adds fresh evidence that the current hard-court version is ready.

⏱️ The recent workload is manageable: Five Cincinnati matches created useful rhythm, but the roughly ten-day gap before this opener reduces the likelihood that the run becomes a fatigue problem.

🔍 Match Breakdown

Cobolli has the stronger form, the higher level of opposition, the better hard-court trend and the recent big-event rhythm. Comesana's first objective is therefore not to outplay Cobolli across every phase; it is to prevent the match from opening up too quickly. A strong first-serve percentage and a clean opening service pattern are essential after the 1-6 first set in his latest match.

Comesana can create pressure if he serves well enough to keep the score level and makes Cobolli generate pace repeatedly from neutral positions. The underdog also took a set from Cobolli in their Monte Carlo meeting, so there is evidence that he can disrupt the favourite for a period. The problem is translating that resistance to hard court, where Comesana's 3-7 recent record and 5-10 last-52-week split are both weak.

Cobolli's winning route is to attack the second serve, keep Comesana from settling into long holds and use his stronger physical and class base over the longer format. He does not need to chase an immediate blowout. If he remains patient, the pressure should accumulate naturally because Comesana has struggled to sustain an ATP-level hard-court standard.

The only meaningful external risk is interruption. A rain delay could break Cobolli's rhythm or allow Comesana to reset after a poor start. In uninterrupted play, the evidence is unusually aligned behind the favourite.

🔮 Prediction

Cobolli should win. Comesana has enough serve and competitive discipline to make individual sets respectable, but there is no supplied form category in which he holds a durable advantage. Cobolli's Cincinnati semifinal, 7-3 recent hard record, 26.6-point CFS edge and superior opposition-quality numbers all point in the same direction.

⚖️ Overall form is neutral: Marozsan is 5-5 in his last ten and 24-26 over the last 52 weeks, producing a 42.5 CFS.

📉 The recent hard window is weak: He is 3-7 across his last ten hard matches despite a balanced 14-14 ATP-hard record over the full last-52-week period.

🧩 The latest result was competitive: Marozsan won the first set before losing a three-set Winston-Salem quarterfinal to Duckworth.

🏟️ He owns the larger main-tour base: Marozsan is 49-44 across his ATP hard career and 64-75 against Top 100 opposition.

🔁 The H2H is negative and recent: Zheng beat him in Cincinnati in August 2026, recovering from a lost opening set and winning the deciding tiebreak emphatically.

🎾 Serving output is adequate: Marozsan averages 4.8 aces per match over the last 52 weeks, slightly below Zheng's 5.7.

Michael Zheng

📈 The raw season is far stronger: Zheng is 6-4 in his last ten, 34-14 over the last 52 weeks and carries a 62.7 raw CFS.

🟦 Most hard success comes below ATP level: He is 16-3 at Challenger/ITF level but only 4-6 at ATP level over the last 52 weeks.

🚨 The latest result triggers a veto: Zheng lost 6-1, 6-3 to Musetti in Cincinnati. The lopsided most-recent hard result activates the fresh-collapse rule.

✅ He has handled the Top 100 reasonably: A 6-7 last-52-week record is credible for his limited tour exposure and compares closely with Marozsan's current percentages.

🔁 The recent H2H is a real positive: The Cincinnati win shows that he can solve this exact opponent on this surface.

⏳ The two-week gap cuts both ways: It offers recovery from Cincinnati but provides no new match evidence to show the collapse has been corrected.

🔍 Match Breakdown

The market, CFS and recent H2H all favour Zheng. Under a normal review, those three aligned signals would create a clear KEEP. The problem is his last hard match: a 6-1, 6-3 loss to Musetti that blocks a positive recommendation under the fresh-collapse rule.

Marozsan has enough experience and rally quality to exploit a hesitant start. He was competitive in Winston-Salem and owns a much deeper ATP-hard résumé. Yet his 3-7 recent hard line prevents the review from simply flipping to the underdog.

Zheng's route is to recreate the Cincinnati pattern, use the confidence of the recent H2H and trust the broader 34-14 season. Marozsan's route is to extend the match beyond that recent memory and force Zheng to prove his level after the Musetti defeat.

The humid best-of-five setting normally rewards the player with the more established tour base, but Marozsan's own current surface form is too weak to turn that into a position. Rain adds further variance to a matchup already split between strong season-long data and a negative last impression.

🔮 Prediction

Zheng remains the marginal winner lean, but no betting position survives. His 62.7 CFS and recent H2H make him more likely to advance; the 6-1, 6-3 collapse prevents endorsement. Marozsan's 3-7 hard trend is too poor to justify the upset side.

WOMAN, 88, CAUGHT SNEAKING A FULL ROAST DINNER INTO THE MOVIES IN HER PURSE

CINCINNATI, OH — Eleanor Voss, 88, was caught sneaking a complete roast dinner, foil tray and all, into a movie theater inside her oversized handbag, quietly unwrapping it once the lights went down for the evening screening.

Theater staff say the smell of roast meat and potatoes drew complaints from nearby patrons within the first fifteen minutes of the film, long before anyone realized where it was coming from.

Packed a full foil tray of roast meat, potatoes, and vegetables in her purse
Waited until the lights dimmed before unwrapping the foil covering
Refused to stop eating even after an usher's flashlight found her
Insisted movie popcorn "doesn't fill you up properly" for a full evening
Continued eating steadily through the entire first act of the film
Offered a nearby stranger a potato "since there was plenty to share"
Told the usher the purse was "just naturally roomy," unrelated to smuggling

Nearby moviegoers reportedly assumed the smell was coming from concessions before realizing it was drifting from several rows away.

Theater manager Priya Anand, ten years with the company, said, "I've caught people sneaking in snacks before. I've never caught someone with an entire roast dinner in a purse."

The foil tray, now empty, declined to comment.

Eleanor has since been asked to stick to theater concessions for all future visits going forward.

text:
CLASS OF 2022 ELIGIBILITY UPDATE. SEPTEMBER 1

A state court in South Carolina issued the first major preliminary injunction denial today, while a new TRO in New York and an aggressive filing in Missouri showed how quickly the legal battlefield continues to splinter.

WHAT MOVED IN COURT

South Carolina / Dalley. The Pickens County Court of Common Pleas denied the Class of 2022 plaintiffs' preliminary injunction request after Monday's hearing. A short written order electronically filed Tuesday morning stated that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate a likelihood of success on the merits. The underlying lawsuit remains alive and the denial can be appealed, but none of the Dalley plaintiffs hold protection from this case tonight.

The practical impact hits Wichita State guard Kenyon Giles immediately. Giles can continue practicing with the team, but without relief from another court he cannot compete. His original nationwide protection disappeared with the August 21 Wisne stay, and the South Carolina ruling failed to replace it.

New York / Amarri Monroe. A New York Supreme Court judge granted Syracuse transfer Amarri Monroe a TRO today following his filing Monday in Onondaga County. Monroe is enrolled at Syracuse with financial aid and NIL agreements tied to basketball, seeking to block the NCAA from enforcing the old four-season limit. The TRO gives him temporary protection to participate while the case moves forward. This is court protection, not NCAA certification.

New York / Roddy Gayle Jr. Former Michigan guard Roddy Gayle Jr. filed in Niagara County Supreme Court against the NCAA and Charlie Baker, seeking a TRO and preliminary injunction for a fifth season. Michigan formally offered him a 2026-27 roster spot conditioned solely on his eligibility, and Gayle is enrolled and practicing. No order has surfaced yet, leaving him as relief requested.

Missouri / Sterling Webb. Webb already holds a TRO against the NCAA, but he asked Judge Ellen Ribaudo to extend equivalent restraints to the University of Missouri and the UM System Board of Curators. His filing argues that the school itself, not the NCAA, certifies eligibility and withholds athletes from play. Webb wants to prevent Missouri from declaring him ineligible, withholding certification, blocking NIL compensation, or barring him from practice and games. Hearing is set for September 2 at 10 a.m. CT. Beating the NCAA in court may still leave an athlete needing an order against his own university.

Kentucky. No new order from Judge Brian Edwards today. Alex Afari and 25 proposed additional plaintiffs, including Seth Trimble, remain under submission following Monday's hearing. The 13 athletes covered by the August 21 TRO remain protected.

WHAT MOVED ON CAMPUS

Virginia Tech / DQ Smith. Former South Carolina safety DQ Smith practiced with Virginia Tech on Tuesday after securing protection in Louisiana's Pyburn case. Because Smith attended an NFL tryout without signing an NFL contract, reporting indicates he satisfies the ACC's separate pro activity rules. The Louisiana preliminary injunction hearing is September 3.

Georgia / Carter Loflin. Loflin voluntarily dismissed his lawsuit without prejudice after Georgia's golf roster deadline passed before a TRO ruling. His attorney cited timing rather than merits. Loflin moves from relief requested to dismissed with no protection.

NEXT 24 HOURS

Wednesday brings the Webb hearing in Missouri at 10 a.m. CT, the six-plaintiff Adams proceeding in Oklahoma, the Trotter federal preliminary injunction hearing for 14 Marshall and Ohio athletes at 1.30 p.m. ET, and the NCAA reply deadline in JPML MDL 3198.

If Butters, Greene, and Marshall arrive, that could leave just 3 main national draft spots and potentially 2 rookie draft spots to fill.

If Port decides to let Butters leave via restricted free agency. They would be expected to gain elite, Band-One compensation in Pick 5 from the AFL instantly, sitting right next to Pick 4.

Under the two-picks rule, because Pick 5 is a compensation pick (and not traded in from another club) and sits right behind Pick 4, if Port do not offload Pick 5, it gets non-optionally eaten up wholly alongside Pick 4 in a Pick 1 bid match on Cochrane.

To avoid this, Port and Geelong can agree to a separate pick trade after Port has firstly opted to take the compensation Pick 5 on offer, sending that Pick 5 to Geelong in a later separate trade.

The Cats would send Port three required first-round selections spanning 2026, 2027, and 2028.

Alongside these, Geelong packages their 2027 and 2028 second-round picks, necessitating a slide back from Port Adelaide to the Cats of their 2027 and 2028 third-round picks, followed by a trade of both clubs' 2027 and 2028 fourth-round picks.

This equates the pick-tier collateral to replenish Geelong’s hand

The Cats could then offer the acquired Pick 5 to St Kilda in exchange for ruckman Rowan Marshall. With Blicavs on an initial 1 year contract and deployable elsewhere Marshall would then partner Edwards.

St Kilda’s 2027 future first might come back to Geelong if the Cats were also to offer a 2027 future second-round pick in return.

The Cats would retain their 25-year-old tall Key Position Defender (KPD) and reserve ruck, Sam De Koning.

Marshall is 30 years old and commands roughly a $900K salary slot, with the Cats by now having freed up more salary capital.

St Kilda natively holds Pick 8 in the 2026 draft, expected to slide to Pick 10. By executing this pick swap, they land Pick 5 to sit next to it—expected to slide to Pick 7.

In isolation, a 30-year-old top-line ruckman normally commands a late first-round or early second-round selection (typically valued between 500–800 points).

However, because St Kilda explicitly brought in Tom De Koning on a massive, long-term, multi-million dollar contract, Marshall’s role has been heavily squeezed.

The Saints free up cap space from Marshall’s contract and use their two top-10 foundational selections to instantly draft two elite open-pool stars.

They may sacrifice their 2027 future first, but gaining Geelong’s 2027 future second gives them the flexible points required to match their own upcoming local NGA talent without entering a points deficit.

WHAT IT IS
- Tesla’s paid autonomous ride service. You book a car in the Robotaxi app. The car drives. There is no human driver on unsupervised rides.
- Live cars today are mostly Model Y. The purpose-built Cybercab is the volume vehicle testers say Tesla is prioritizing.
- Camera-only vision. Tesla VP of AI Ashok Elluswamy: no lidar, radar, or HD maps required for safe operation on this stack.
- This how-to merges the public Robotaxi service folder with Owning Robotaxi Fleet (owner / private-fleet economics). Not Cybercab-only bookmarks.

HOW IT WORKS
- Download the Tesla Robotaxi app and join the waitlist. Official robotaxi (Sep 2025): app is available to all; access expands over time.
- Book the ride in Tesla’s app. Elon: Tesla will not partner with Uber or Lyft. “We will have enough demand.”
- Unsupervised means no safety driver. Supervised cities still have a person in the car.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): service hours are 6am to 10pm, 7 days/week. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger. Upgraded vehicle distribution and routing so you wait less.
- Testers: you can change destination and keep the same trip for multiple stops.
- Cars return to a depot or homebase and park themselves (Houston footage).
- Ashok: FSD v15 is already running on Model Y robotaxis and will run on Cybercab.
- Testers: Tesla is limiting Model Y conversions to prioritize Cybercab, built with an unboxed modular process.
- Testers (Aug 24): Tesla expects Cybercab to replace Model Ys in the Robotaxi fleet over time and become the highest-volume vehicle there. Testers flag Sept 3 / 9/3 as the Cybercab strategy moment. Austin public Cybercab rides described as “imminent.”

HOW TO USE
- Official robotaxi: download the app, join the waitlist.
- Official robotaxi (Aug 27): rides run 6am to 10pm every day. Unsupervised fleet is a lot bigger; routing upgrade is meant to cut wait time.
- Testers: booking is in the app. One Orlando rider paid with an X Money card.
- Tesla site (as quoted): app in 29 languages; service animals; space for some wheelchairs and assistive devices.
- Testers: vehicles in Nevada must be marked “Robotaxi.”
- After the Aug 20 Nevada approval, testers say Tesla still has to finish vehicle inspections, insurance, and published rates before paid rides start there.

OWNING / FLEET (from Owning Robotaxi Fleet dump)
- Elon (Feb 2026, also in Robotaxi folder): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.
- Fleet testers frame the network like Airbnb for cars: owner adds vehicle; Tesla handles software, routing, payments, rider experience; platform fee often modeled ~25–35%; owner keeps the rest after operating costs (tester).
- Fleet / Teslaconomics (Mar 2026): ~$30k/yr net profit per Robotaxi to owner is a base-case assumption from analyst models + Tesla long-term vision — after platform fee, charging, tires, maintenance, insurance, cleaning. No official real-world owner earnings in this dump. Profit/mile chatter ~$0.25–$0.50 after costs at 50k–100k+ miles/yr in high-demand areas.
- Fleet / Teslaconomics: Cybercab cost chatter ~$25k–$30k; Elon told that tester production was starting in ~1 month (Mar 2026 context — treat as dated tester claim). Rough capital for a ~$1M/yr fleet ~$850k–$1M in vehicles (tester arithmetic).
- Fleet / chamath: intends to buy and deploy large fleets nationally when possible; expects payback and positive FCF in under 2 years (tester / investor claim, not Official Tesla).
- Fleet / BrianRoemmele: “all in” on buying into the owning-fleet thesis now; separate Optimus ownership program mentioned but not published in this dump.
- Fleet / tslaming (Mar 2026): then only 8 unsupervised Austin robotaxis — historical; do not use as current fleet size (Robotaxi dump Aug 23 tester: 908 total).
- Testers / Teslaconomics (Aug 25, Robotaxi folder): “owning your own Tesla Robotaxi fleet can one day make you financially free.” Still a tester slogan — no Official owner-earnings number in this dump.
- CONFLICT / caution: owner earnings, Cybercab sticker, ROI, and payback are tester models. Dump explicitly says none of it is guaranteed. Do not treat as Official Tesla guidance.

SERVICE AREA / CITIES
- Unsupervised (no safety driver), as listed May 2026: Austin, TX (launched Jun 22, 2025); Dallas, TX and Houston, TX (launched Apr 18, 2026).
- Supervised (safety driver), as listed May 2026: SF Bay Area, CA (launched Apr 18, 2026).

- Testers (Aug 27 travel_invest): recap of Official hours post lists 6 target cities — Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa. Tester translation, not a new Official city list.
- Nevada (Aug 20, 2026): full network permit for paid public service. Start small in Clark County / Las Vegas; Tesla can expand elsewhere in the state after notifying the commission.
- Testers (Aug 23): Nevada approved Tesla for up to 5,000 autonomous vehicles, up from a 10-car interim limit. Tesla said it would be “extremely happy” to have around 2,500 running within a year.
- Testers (May 2026) said Tesla was also aiming at Phoenix, Miami, Orlando, Tampa.
- Hiring and test-vehicle posts (treat as signals, not live service): Arizona, Florida, Washington, New York, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, California, D.C., plus a Germany Arzfeld pilot with a safety driver and Japan Kanagawa job listings.

ACCESS AND PLANS
- Official: Robotaxi app waitlist. Access expands as cities open.
- Testers (Aug 27 WorldlyReviewer): received an email from Tesla advertising Robotaxi. Tester report of Tesla marketing, not a new Official service announcement.
- Elon (Feb 2026): Tesla owners will be able to add their cars to the Robotaxi network; Tesla collects 25% of revenue.

SAFETY

FLEET AND INFRASTRUCTURE

text:
**When the Streets Become Rivers: A Case for Dual Sanitation**

Prof Waqar Hussain 

When some 290 millimetres of rain fell upon Islamabad, the city did not merely get wet; it came unstitched. Streets turned into nullahs, and the nullahs into rivers. Water, with no honourable exit, stole into houses and laid waste to household goods. Cars stood half-drowned; those caught in the current might float like boats. It was an old story in a new downpour. Not long before, the same monsoon fury had made a wreck of Raja Bazaar. Many rushed to score political points; few offered a remedy that might last longer than a news cycle.

If the object is not merely to wring one’s hands but to grasp the nettle, one proposal deserves a hearing.

During training after the competitive examination, this scribe was assigned research on “Solid-Waste Management”. A study of sanitation systems made one fact plain as day: in developed societies the rule is a dual, or separate, sewer system—one pipe for household sewage, another solely for stormwater.

That modern dual system first took practical root in the United States. Engineer George E. Waring Jr. built an early separate scheme at Lenox, Massachusetts, in 1875, and in 1880 laid the celebrated system at Memphis, Tennessee. Earlier still, in the 1840s and 1850s, Edwin Chadwick and John Phillips in England had argued for the same principle; it was in America that it first became civic practice on a notable scale.

Today the dual system is the gold standard for new development across much of the developed world—the United States, Canada, most of Europe, Japan, Australia, South Korea, and many others. Older cities still labour under combined sewers, but the campaign to uncouple them goes on. In one form or another the arrangement has been adopted in more than fifty countries.

The early phases of Defence in Lahore were built on this very principle. There, even a monsoon cloudburst can run off in minutes through dedicated rain drains. Where a single, combined system remains, stormwater has no proper channel; it mixes with household waste, chokes the pipes, and comes home to roost as flood. The result is Raja Bazaar as a lake, E-11 as a river—all over again.

If the will to solve the problem is genuine, let dual sanitation be laid in Twin Cities . Otherwise the same spectacle will return with every monsoon, as surely as night follows day.🙏🙏🙏

Could there be a guarantee of high yield performance

No, there is absolutely no guarantee that X Money’s high-yield performance will remain at 6% APY permanently.
Like virtually all high-yield cash accounts, the interest rate offered by X Money is strictly a variable rate, meaning the platform reserves the right to change, lower, or remove the yield at any moment without prior notice. [1]
If you are looking at the long-term reality of this yield, consider the following structural limitations:

📊 The Hidden Realities of the 6% APY
•The Rate Is a Corporate Subsidy: Right now, the broader U.S. financial system cannot naturally produce a 6% return on risk-free, FDIC-insured demand deposits. Standard high-yield savings accounts at competitive online banks top out around 4.10% to 4.50% APY. This means Elon Musk's broader corporate ecosystem is actively subsidizing the extra two percentage points as an expensive marketing campaign to acquire customers. Tech companies historically slash these promotional subsidies once they hit their user growth targets. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
•Tied to the Federal Reserve: High-yield bank accounts base their numbers on the Federal Reserve's benchmark interest rates. If the Fed cuts interest rates across the banking sector, the underlying yield that X's partner, Cross River Bank, can actually earn will drop. This will force X to either burn more corporate cash to maintain the 6% sticker price or lower the yield to match the broader economy. [1, 2, 3]
•State-Level Disruption: A yield is never guaranteed if local regulators step in. As mentioned previously, New York and Massachusetts residents are blocked from earning interest on X Money due to localized money transmitter licensing rules, proving how quickly geographic variables can alter your expected returns. [1]

🔒 What Is Guaranteed?
While the performance rate isn't fixed, the safety of your principal deposit is guaranteed up to legal limits. Because your cash is swept into FDIC-insured partner networks via Cross River Bank, you are mathematically guaranteed against losing your core balance up to $10 million if the platform or the banking backend faces financial distress. < Be Joseph Choate
< Born 1832, Salem, Massachusetts
< Your ancestors arrived on the Mayflower. You arrive at Harvard.
< Graduate first in your class, 1852
< Harvard Law follows. You finish in two years.
< Move to New York City with $200 and a letter of introduction
< The letter opens one door. You open the rest.
< Join a small firm. Within five years, you are the firm.
< Evarts, Southmayd & Choate becomes the address for serious money
< You marry Caroline Sterling. Four daughters, one son.
< The Gilded Age arrives. So do your clients.
< Standard Oil. AT&T. The Northern Pacific Railway.
< You argue before the Supreme Court like other men argue at dinner
< Twelve appearances become twenty. Twenty become fifty.
< Final count: over 250 arguments before the Court
< You win most of them. The losses you dismiss as judicial error.
< 1895: Pollock v. Farmers' Loan & Trust Co.
< The federal income tax is unconstitutional, you argue. The Court agrees.
< Five to four. The Sixteenth Amendment will take eighteen years to undo it.
< You call the income tax "communistic." The papers love it.
< Reformers call you the lawyer who killed fair taxation
< You call it property rights. The retainer clears either way.
< President McKinley offers you the Supreme Court seat
< You decline. Private practice pays better.
< 1899: Ambassador to the Court of St. James's
< You represent America to Queen Victoria in silk knee breeches
< The press adores you. The diplomats trust you.
< Return home 1905. Resume arguing. Resume winning.
< Die 1917, age eighty-four, still working

text:
Great question

Nothing that my outer heart hoped for. I did not awake to find a golden cybertruck in my driveway. Nothing like that happened. 

Or was it… everything that my inner heart desires happened. Gods story remains True, testified by His creation. 

Depends on perspective, doesn’t it? Yesterday, the sun rose in the east and set in the west. Great place to start and finish! There’s a Hope for tomorrow and a Joy over all the earth. 

For Jonah, God appointed the shade from vine to protect from the powerful sun, He appointed the worm to wither the plant, and He appointed a scorching east wind. Jonah was angry, angry enough to die. 

We pity the plant for which we did not make, yet God has pity on the people of the city. I don’t think it’s too bold to extend Gods mercy for Nineveh to Memphis. 

God is unchanging, and we can rejoice in the Lord and his great faithfulness, every day, and the great blessing he is offered us, free of charge. 

Old wisdom: 
Summer and winter and springtime and harvest,
Sun, moon, and stars in their courses above
Join with all nature in manifold witness
To thy great faithfulness, mercy, and love.

Pardon for sin and a peace that endureth,
Thine own dear presence to cheer and to guide;
Strength for today and bright hope for tomorrow,
Blessings all mine and ten thousand beside.

Great is thy faithfulness, O God, my Father;
There is no shadow of turning with thee.
Thou changest not, thy compassions, they fail not;
As thou hast been, thou forever wilt be.

I wonder what tomorrow will bring?

text:
“Political bravery”? No, Susan Aitken, this is an attack on workers https://t.co/YaytcqqrP8 

This piece by Richie Venton, SSP trade union organiser, was originally published in the Scottish National, 01/09/2026.

“We’ve had enough!” chanted several hundred council workers at a hastily organised, angry demonstration outside the meeting of Glasgow City Administration Committee (CAC) on 20 August.

Members of the council workers’ unions – Unison, GMB and UNITE – warned the assembled councillors of the political consequences if they went ahead with their Pay and Grading package, involving totally inadequate compensation for decades of wage discrimination against women workers, and absolute pay cuts for thousands of them. Workers blasted out: “Vote for this today – no votes in May!”

All ten SNP and all three Scottish Green Party councillors on the CAC committee ignored the workers’ voices. They voted through a grading structure which means 26% of council workers get no pay rise, and another 11% suffer absolute pay cuts. That’s over 2,500 workers, 60% of them women, with lower-paid roles disproportionately impacted. The SNP and Scottish Green councillors voted to slash workers’ wages by up £11,500 annually – worse still than the £10,000 previously predicted.

To sweeten the poison, the SNP/Green alliance increased the pay protection period from their original 6 months to a year – still presenting workers with a cliff-edge fall in incomes in April 2028.

A perverse outcome to the 20-year-long battle for equal pay.

As I write this column, workers are receiving written confirmation of the pay cuts they’ve been verbally notified of. I know of women in tears after being told they face a £9,000 pay cut, despite increased workload and regularly working unpaid overtime. Or care workers and school support staff worried sick at facing £2,000 to £3,000 loss of annual wages. Many of those hit are women who fought against the Labour council for equal pay from 2006 onwards.

SNP council leader Susan Aitken had the gall to appeal for “political bravery” in voting for these measures. She insisted “this is a Glasgow problem, made in Glasgow”, declaring there was no chance of (and no case for) approaching the Scottish government for what she contemptuously called “a bailout” – when in fact central governments at Holyrood and Westminster have robbed Glasgow of £500million in funding in recent years.

The SNP and Scottish Greens should hang their heads in shame.

But Labour’s protestations reek of the rankest hypocrisy, since they created this decades-long pay injustice!

Between 2007-2017, the then Labour-dominated council ferociously fought against the demands of women workers for equal pay. Trade union-funded Labour councillors squandered at least £2.5million of council taxpayers’ money on legal actions to block the justified demand for equal pay for work of equal value.

The SNP won a big mandate in the 2017 council elections by promising to end Labour’s grotesque injustice. But after 10 months of fruitless talks in 21 separate meetings, it took strike action by 8,000 predominantly women workers in October 2018 to get results against the crime of female-dominated roles in cleaning, catering and care being paid up to £3-an-hour less than workers in comparable, male-dominated jobs. That heroic collective action – with the solidarity of male cleansing workers, who refused to cross women’s picket lines – won payments totalling £770million to about 19,000 workers.

The SNP/Scottish Greens are now trampling past promises in the muck.

The council will backdate compensation to 2023, but base the amount paid to each worker on their entry level pay to the job – not their actual pay at each point since.

Whereas the councillors estimate their compensation package will cost £76million, they reject the joint unions’ demand for full backdated equal pay because – according to them – it would cost £133million. So, by their own figures, the council are robbing workers of £57million in compensatory back-payments.

As an outrageous, dictatorial means of imposing these measures, the Pay and Grading Report – agreed by the SNP and Scottish Greens – furthermore states that if collective agreement cannot be reached, they may consider “other lawful options”- including “dismissal of existing contracts and offers of re-engagement on revised terms and conditions.”

Ever heard of that before? That’s the notorious method deployed by British Gas, Birmingham Labour council and many other employers, endorsed by the previous Tory government, commonly known as ‘fire-and-rehire’.

It’s a bludgeon to bully workers, break the backs of the unions, and impose worsened conditions.

It’s a method Westminster’s Labour government promised to outlaw, but have not properly done, delaying reforms to it until January 2027, and then leaving loopholes whereby employers can still put this machine-gun to workers’ heads “in cases of genuine financial difficulty”.

All of which may help explain why the SNP and Scottish Greens rammed through a partial Pay and Grading package, excluding over 5,000 other council staff, conscious of these deadlines and get-out clauses.

The underlying problem is totally inadequate funding of councils by central governments, and the regressive, inadequate funding methods they deploy for local government.

There are only two ways to implement equal pay for comparable jobs; levelling up, or levelling down. But the former requires additional funds, otherwise workers are hammered with pay cuts – robbing Peter (and often Petra) to pay Pauline.

Months ago, COSLA estimated a £1billion shortfall in Scottish government funding to the 32 local authority budgets this year and next (£530million in 2026/7 alone).

Well over £500million has been stolen in funding from Glasgow City Council by the Holyrood government in recent years, as they devolved Westminster’s destructive austerity.

Instead of lying down in prostration, accepting that fate, Glasgow city councillors should agree a revised package with the trade unions that is fully equality-proofed, with no loss of earnings for any worker, with full compensation for years of appalling, gender-based pay inequality – and mount a campaign alongside the workforce to win back some of the stolen millions off the Scottish Government, to pay for it. That is what Scottish Socialist Party councillors would do.

Alongside that, they should adopt the Scottish Socialist Party’s long-established alternative to the regressive, totally inadequate Council Tax, and demand that Holyrood urgently introduces the SSP’s progressive, income-based Scottish Service Tax.

Our most recent calculations (based on 2024 data) prove this would double this source of funding to Scotland’s councils, from £2.7billion Council Tax to £5.3billion in Scottish Service Tax – while only charging more to the richest 20% of people.

This battle is far from over. It took the 1968 Fords Dagenham sewing machinists’ strike to enforce introduction of the 1970 Equal Pay Act, and 50 years later the Glasgow equal pay strike to win initial compensation. Assuming the unions win members’ votes for strike action, a mighty struggle for proper funding from the Scottish government can be won.

SSP members inside and outside the council workforce will help build united resistance to these outrageous attacks, in defence of equal pay and compensation without detriment to the wages of a single council worker.

And in next year’s council elections, the SSP will offer a fighting socialist alternative of equal pay, reversal of service cuts, and taxation of the rich to transform the lives of workers and their communities. Workers deserve genuine socialists to represent them.

Richie speaks at a demonstration in support of the council workers, 20/08/2026.

The post “Political bravery”? No, Susan Aitken, this is an attack on workers appeared first on Scottish Socialist Party.

text:
The Florida Commission on Ethics has found probable cause that Randy Fine took $20,000 in prohibited gifts.
The money came from his own political committee, Friends of Randy Fine. It went to a Melbourne attorney hired to keep him out of two depositions he did not want to sit for. One of those is the deposition he was dodging when he called the Sheriff's Office on a process server and hid under his desk.

He never reported a dollar of it as a gift.

The investigation was finished in December 2024. The Commission's own advocate recommended probable cause on January 6, 2025.

The vote did not happen for another 599 days.
For two and a half years his attorney told the Commission he could not appear. Congress was in session. Congress was not in session but he had a travel day. He was in South America. He was in Israel. He was at a conference in Denver. The Commission finally offered to move the whole thing to the August 2026 congressional recess and asked which Friday would be convenient for him.

He picked August 28. Ten days after the primary he was running in.

Then on August 12 he tried to move that one too, and offered to waive his right to attend in person only if the case was dismissed.

The chair denied it, in part because eight days earlier Fine had asked a federal judge to let his Chief of Staff stand in for him at a mediation, citing the exact same congressional duties.

He did not show up on August 28. His lawyer appeared for him, which the rules allowed the entire time.
Meanwhile the older case, the one where he called Jennifer Jenkins a whore and put Special Olympics funding on the "veto list," has been sitting since 2022. The Commission found probable cause on that in April 2023. Three years and four months later it still has not been heard, and at the same August meeting half the allegations were thrown out under a law passed while the case sat idle.

text:
Martin County State Attorney Thomas Bakkedahl on Wednesday defended prosecutors’ decision to offer Tiger Woods a plea deal, saying they lacked sufficient evidence to prove he was impaired during his March 27 rollover crash on Jupiter Island, Florida.

Bakkedahl called it a particularly difficult DUI to prove since Woods refused a urinalysis at the scene, so prosecutors were unable to establish what was in his system. Woods admitted taking Vicodin, a controlled substance under state and federal law, but two toxicologists reviewed police reports, body camera video, and pharmacy records and found ‘insufficient proof of impairment,’ in part because of Woods' documented tolerance to the drug after years of use following multiple back surgeries.

A judge outlined the agreement Wednesday. The DUI charge was reduced to reckless driving and the refusal charge was also reduced. Woods pleaded no contest to both, was fined $1,500, and had his license suspended for five years. He avoids jail time, but violating the terms of the deal could put him back in front of a judge.

The case stemmed from a March crash in which Woods rolled his SUV  after clipping a pickup truck hauling pressure-cleaning equipment. Police said he failed a field sobriety test, refused a urine test and admitted to taking "a few pills.” Officers found two hydrocodone pills in his pocket. A breathalyzer detected no alcohol, and no one was injured.

Bakkedahl closed the press conference with a message for Woods, saying, “Of all the people in the world who should not get behind the wheel of a car, it's the gentleman who is one of the most recognizable faces on the planet.”

text:
I honestly cannot believe how many people who call themselves conservatives are announcing that they will vote for David Jolly simply because they hate Byron Donalds.

You do not have to like Byron. I certainly do not. I did not support him in the primary & my problems with him did not magically disappear when he won.

But before you vote for Jolly, understand exactly what you are voting for.

1. CODIFYING ROE & CASEY
Jolly wants Florida to codify the Roe & Casey abortion framework into state law.
2. BANNING SO-CALLED ASSAULT WEAPONS
Jolly wants Florida to ban the sale of firearms Democrats classify as assault weapons.
3. GUN LICENSING & MORE RED FLAG LAWS
He supports universal background checks, wants Florida to consider gun licensing & wants to expand red flag laws.
4. MEDICAID EXPANSION
Jolly wants Florida to expand Medicaid & dramatically increase the government’s role in healthcare.
5. RESTRICTING SCHOOL CHOICE
He wants school vouchers means-tested & private schools accepting vouchers placed under additional government mandates. That means fewer families qualifying & more state control over private education.
6. MORE GOVERNMENT SPENDING
Jolly calls for a dramatic increase in state spending on public schools without clearly explaining where all that additional money will come from.
7. A STATE CATASTROPHE INSURANCE FUND
He wants natural-disaster risk removed from private insurance companies & placed under a state-backed catastrophe fund.
8. STATE-BACKED CONDOMINIUM LOANS
Jolly wants the state to provide interest-free loans to condominium owners & associations. Government-backed loans involve public money & public risk.
9. GOVERNMENT-MANDATED RENEWABLE ENERGY
He wants Florida to require greater use of renewable-energy technology by public utilities & adopt a statewide climate & sustainability agenda.
10. MAKING FLORIDA’S CONSTITUTION EASIER TO CHANGE
Jolly wants constitutional amendments easier to place on the ballot. He also says the governor should fight to enact any amendment receiving more than 50% of the vote. Florida currently requires 60%. That 60% protects our Constitution from being rewritten by a temporary, razor-thin majority.
11. EXPANDING LOCAL CONTROL OVER POLICING
Jolly wants more local control over community policing while placing specific emphasis on racial & immigrant disparities in the criminal justice system.
12. REVERSING FLORIDA’S APPROACH TO GENDER-RELATED MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR MINORS
Jolly says government should stay out of gender-related medical decisions made by families & doctors. For accuracy, he has not publicly said he supports surgeries on young children. What he supports is removing government from these decisions involving minors instead of maintaining Florida’s current restrictions.
13. OPPOSING REPUBLICAN IMMIGRATION POLICIES
Jolly has criticized Republican immigration enforcement, arguing that it tightens the labor supply & increases costs. His campaign says Florida should embrace immigrant communities but offers very little detail about illegal immigration, cooperation with federal enforcement or sanctuary policies.

This is not a collection of Republican accusations. Most of it comes directly from David Jolly’s own campaign platform & public statements.

You have every right to vote for whomever you choose. But hatred for Byron Donalds does not transform David Jolly’s agenda into a conservative agenda. A vote against Byron is still a vote for Jolly. It is a vote for abortion protections, gun restrictions, Medicaid expansion, more government spending, climate mandates, weaker protections for Florida’s Constitution & the reversal of policies conservatives spent years putting into place.

If you support all of that, own it. But if you vote for Jolly while calling yourself a conservative, you need to change your label because you are not conservative by any stretch of the imagination.

There is nothing Jolly about Jolly.

🚨 A first-time drug possession charge in Illinois is almost always a FELONY — but Section 410 probation (720 ILCS 570/410) can end the case with no conviction at all.
 
 Under 720 ILCS 570/402, knowingly possessing a controlled substance without a valid prescription — less than a gram of cocaine or heroin, or a few oxycodone, Xanax, or Adderall pills that aren't yours — is a Class 4 felony carrying 1 to 3 years in prison and fines up to $25,000. A conviction also triggers a mandatory driver's license suspension by the Illinois Secretary of State, even when no driving was involved. For eligible first-time offenders charged with Class 4 felony possession, 410 probation is a critical lifeline: successfully complete the probation term and the charge is DISMISSED — no conviction ever enters your record. Illinois offers related alternatives too, including Second Chance Probation and TASC, but eligibility rules are strict and these programs are generally a one-time opportunity you cannot afford to waste.

A few random facts:

Brazil (which was more populous than the American South in 1861) did not ban slavery until the 1880s. Nor did Cuba. It was far from a smooth process for them, either.

In the 1840s and 1850s, state-level black-exclusion laws passed in Illinois, Indiana, and elsewhere with large majorities.

Lincoln endorsed protecting slavery in the Southern states in perpetuity via a Constitutional amendment, but Southern states still wanted to leave despite that.

In the early 1800s, Northern and British bankers began favoring slaves as collateral over land. Planters needed loans every year to fund the planting of next year’s crop. The collateral preference indirectly discouraged paying workers for farm labor and contributed significantly to the industrialization of slavery in the Deep South in the early to mid 1800s. No Northern or British bankers offered Southern planters a debt jubilee to free their slaves.

History is complex. Even now, slavery continues to exist and contributes to the creation of the machine you are typing on and probably some of the clothes you are wearing. What are you doing to end it?

☢️ ESKALERING AV USA-IRAN-KRIGET (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): Amerikanska styrkor lanserade nya attacker mot Iran, inklusive en attack i hamnstaden Sirik som träffade en bröllopsfest och dödade 4–5 civila enligt iransk statsmedia och bekräftat av BBC/Al Jazeera. Iran har vedergällt: Shahed-136-loitering-ammunition slog mot en amerikansk militäranläggning vid Erbils internationella flygplats i irakiska Kurdistan; minst en avvärjdes över Khalifan. Explosioner rapporterade över Bahrain med flyglarmssirener. IRGC hävdar man slog mot en amerikansk bas i Jordanien, vilket USA förnekar. Trump skrev att USA har "nästan total kontroll över Hormuzsundet" och uttalade uttryckligen att man inte söker ett iranskt avtal, och ramade in konflikten som ett pågående strategiskt mål snarare än en väg till förhandling.

☢️ IAEA BEKRÄFTAR ATT SYRIEN BYGGDE HEMLIG KÄRNREAKTOR (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): IAEA bekräftade att Syrien under Assad byggde en kärnreaktor i Deir az-Zor, en stor spridningsavslöjande med implikationer för det post-Assad-Syriens stabilitet och regionalt kärnvapenansvarsutkrävande. Denna reaktor förstördes med största sannolikhet av en israelisk flygattack 2007, men formell IAEA-bekräftelse bär nu diplomatisk tyngd.

🎯 RYSK-IRANSK MISSILTEKNOLOGIÖVERFÖRING (MÅTTLIG KONFIDENSGRAD): Financial Times rapporterar att Ryssland i hemlighet hjälpt Iran utveckla överljudskryssningsmissilteknik sedan 2023 under Program C430L, potentiellt landets mest betydande militärtekniköverföring till Teheran, direkt relevant i takt med att konflikten eskalerar.

⚡ IRAKISKT INTERNETAVBROTT — PÅGÅENDE (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): IODA-data visar att Irak upplevt en kritisk, multikälls internetstörning i 7-plus sammanhängande dagar, med en 65-procentig nedgång i ping-nåbara nätverk. Detta är allvarligt och sannolikt konfliktrelaterat, vilket hämmar civil kommunikation och komplicerar stridsskadebedömning.

🌊 TROPISKA STORMEN EDOUARD GÖR LANDFALL I SYDÖSTRA TEXAS (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): Edouards centrum passerade över Beaumont-storstadsområdet som en 50-knops storm, vilket förde byiga vindar och kraftigt regn till sydöstra Texas. Skyfallsvarningar aktiva över södra New Jersey och Pennsylvania från separata stormsystem.

☢️ PENTAGON FÖRHANDSVISAR SATSNING PÅ TAKTISKA KÄRNVAPEN (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): Försvarsdepartementets tjänstemän förhandsvisade ett skifte i amerikanska riktlinjer för kärnvapenanvändning som betonar taktiska/begränsade kärnvapen, sammanfallande med att Trump drar ner amerikansk-sydkoreanska militärövningar, en anmärkningsvärd samtidig strategisk signal.

⚡ CISA UTFÄRDAR KRITISK ICS-VARNING — ROCKWELL RSLINX (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): CVSS 9,2/10-sårbarheter (CVE-2026-9621/9622/9624/9625) i RSLinx Classic ≤4.50 tillåter fjärr-, oautentiserad överbelastningsattack mot industriella styrsystem. Globalt utplacerat inom kritisk tillverkning. Patcha till version 4.60 omedelbart.

⚓ USS ABRAHAM LINCOLN (CVN-72) ANLÄNDER TILL THAILAND EFTER UTPLACERING I MELLANÖSTERN (MÅTTLIG KONFIDENSGRAD): AP bekräftar att Lincoln anlände till östra Thailand efter utplacering i Mellanöstern. CVN-73 (George Washington) och CVN-77 (Bush) förblir i Arabiska havet-regionen.

🎯 TYSKLAND ANKLAGAR RYSSLAND FÖR DRÖNARATTACKFÖRSÖK MOT UKRAINSKT AN-124-LASTPLAN (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): Tyskland anklagade formellt Ryssland för att ha riktat in sig på ett ukrainskt lastflygplan, med separata incidenter riktade mot Tysklands elnät, vilket indikerar breddande hybridkrigföringsfotavtryck i Europa.

🦠 EBOLAUTBROTTET I DR KONGO EXPANDERAR SNABBT (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD): 5 794 bekräftade fall, 2 786 dödsfall (48,1 procent dödlighet) över 60 hälsozoner i 6 provinser. Det största ebolautbrottet som någonsin rapporterats i DR Kongo förblir ett internationellt hot mot människors hälsa. Spridning accelererande.

REGIONALA HUVUDPUNKTER

MELLANÖSTERN
Aktiva USA-Iran-fientligheter är regionens definierande kris. Amerikanska attacker mot iranskt territorium (inklusive bröllopsfestincidenten i Sirik) har utlöst iransk vedergällning över flera skådeplatser: Irak (Erbil), Bahrain, och påstådda attacker i Jordanien. Amerikanska styrkor förstörde två IRGC-fartyg som lade minor i Hormuzsundet och slog mot en luftvärnsanläggning i Bandar Abbas. Två hangarfartygsstyrkor (CVN-73, CVN-77) förblir i Arabiska havet. Iraks internetinfrastruktur är allvarligt försämrad. Resevarningar för Irak förblir nivå 4 (resa inte dit); Förenade Arabemiraten, Kuwait och Qatar är på nivå 3. FN:s säkerhetsråds franska ordförandeskap har placerat Iran, Haiti och Sudan på sin septemberagenda.

EUROPA
Ryssland hotade formellt att intensifiera attacker mot Ukraina (Putins SCO-uttalanden). FN:s generalförsamling höll en akutdebatt om Ukraina, med generalförsamlingens ordförande som varnade att "inget säkert utrymme finns kvar". Tyskland anklagade Ryssland för ett försök till drönarattack mot ett ukrainskt AN-124 och noterade separata attacker mot tysk elinfrastruktur. Natos övning Saber Junction 26 fortsätter vid Ramstein. Estland håller ett presidentval idag (2 september). Delstatsvalet i Sachsen-Anhalt följer 6 september; Berlin och Mecklenburg-Vorpommern 20 september tillsammans med ryska lagstiftande val.

AMERIKA
Tropiska stormen Edouard gjorde landfall över Beaumont, Texas. Aktiva tornadovarningar i South Dakota/Nebraska under natten. Skyfallsvarningar över New Jersey, Pennsylvania och Utah. FEMA DR-4933 täcker 21 countyn i Indiana från augustis översvämning. Aktiva branddeklarationer i Indiana och Texas pågående. Ett nationellt nödläge för säkerheten i det storskaliga elnätet förklarades 31 augusti genom presidentdekret. Trumps Truth Social-inlägg omramar uttryckligen mellanårsvalsbudskapet kring "kapitalism mot socialism" med 9 veckor kvar till valen till representanthuset/senaten den 3 november.

ASIEN-STILLAHAVSOMRÅDET
USS Abraham Lincoln anlände till Thailand efter utplacering i Mellanöstern, en betydande rotationssignal. Kinas JL-3 SLBM-test i öppet hav (juli) fortsätter ge återklang i strategiska kretsar. Amerikanska KC-46A-tankflygplan verksamma i Mellanöstern-regionen som stöd för pågående attacker. Tropiska stormarna Marie-26 (östra Stilla havet, nära Mexiko) och Krovanh-26 (nordvästra Stilla havet, nära Japan) aktiva men på grön varningsnivå.

AFRIKA
Ebolautbrottet (Bundibugyo-viruset) i DR Kongo: 5 794 fall, 2 786 dödsfall, nu spritt över 60 hälsozoner i 6 provinser, PHEIC-status. Sudans konflikt humanitär nödsituation pågående. FIRMS-satellitbranddata visar förhöjda termiska anomalier över Sydafrikas Gauteng-provins.

MARKNADSIMPLIKATIONER

📈 WTI-råolja +7,1 procent (91,83 dollar): minläggningsincidenten i Hormuzsundet plus amerikanska attacker mot luftvärnsanläggningen i Bandar Abbas plus den deklarerade amerikanska "nästan totala kontrollen" över Hormuz driver akut oro för utbudsstörning. Ytterligare eskalering skulle snabbt kunna driva WTI mot intervallet 95–100 dollar. (HÖG KONFIDENSGRAD)

📉 Aktier brett ner: S&P 500 -0,71 procent, Nasdaq -1,03 procent, Russell 2000 -1,23 procent. Risk-off-sentiment på eskaleringen i Mellanöstern. VIX +9,5 procent till 16,34, förhöjd men inte panikterritorium, vilket antyder att marknaderna prissätter en begränsad konflikt. (MÅTTLIG KONFIDENSGRAD)

📉 Guld -1,8 procent (4 351 dollar): kontraintuitivt fallande trots konflikten, möjligen vinsthemtagning efter tidigare säker hamn-rusning, eller dollarstyrka.

USD-index +0,35 procent: måttlig efterfrågan på dollar som säker hamn i linje med risk-off-positionering.

Medvind för försvars-/energisektorn: Boeing, Raytheon, Lockheed och oljebolag gynnas sannolikt. Sjöfartsförsäkringsbolag möter förhöjda premier för transiter genom Hormuzsundet.

Feds septembermöte (15–16 september): Polymarket prissätter 40,5 procents sannolikhet för ingen räntesänkning, cirka 59 procents sannolikhet för någon sänkning. Olje-/inflationsdata från konflikten skulle kunna komplicera en sänkning. G20:s finansministrars kommuniké enligt uppgift inte överenskommen, signal om splittrad samordning.

Rockwell Automation ICS-sårbarhet: om utnyttjad mot kritisk tillverkningsinfrastruktur skulle försörjningskedjestörningar kunna följa. Patchningsbrådska kritisk.

INDIKATORER ATT BEVAKA (NÄSTA 24–48 TIMMAR)

Rapporter om transit genom Hormuzsundet: varje ytterligare minläggningsförsök, incidenter med handelsfartyg, eller IRGC-marin aktivitet kommer vara ledande indikatorer på om Iran försöker stänga/störa sundet, den högsta ekonomiska eskaleringsrisken. Bevaka USNI:s flottspårare för omplacering av hangarfartyg.

Skadebedömning av amerikansk bas i Jordanien: Pentagon förnekar att baser träffades i Jordanien; IRGC hävdar offer. Oberoende verifiering (satellitbilder, OSINT) av faktisk skada kommer avgöra det politiska trycket för ytterligare amerikansk eskalering eller nedtrappningsöverturer.

Irans inrikes stabilitet / Trumps "res er upp"-signal: Trump uppmanade uttryckligen det iranska folket att "resa sig och kämpa", vilket antyder en regimförändringsinramning. Bevaka indikatorer på inre iransk oro, offentliga uttalanden från revolutionsgardet, och om FN:s säkerhetsråd (franskt ordförandeskap) sammankallar en akutsession om Iran.

IAEA:s efterspel kring den syriska reaktorn: om Israel, USA eller post-Assad syriska myndigheter formellt svarar på IAEA:s bekräftelse av Deir az-Zor-reaktorn, och om det utlöser en bredare session i IAEA:s styrelse.

Edouards inlandsbana + översvämningspåverkan i Texas: bevaka NHC-besked för intensitetsavtagande och regnackumulering i redan mättade områden. FEMA-insatsökningar sannolika givet befintliga aktiva katastrofdeklarationer i Indiana och Texas.
