The crater energy range “1 µm \(\sim\) nJ to 100 µm \(\sim\) mJ” is Nagel’s, but the citation in the source list is wrong: it is *J. Condensed Matter Nucl. Sci.* **10** (2013) 1–14, not vol. 13 (2014) 443.

Fences at the end of Part 2 are the right fences. Keep them verbatim.

---  ## Q1 — branching or only binding?

**Only a binding statement.** Paper 9, as you describe it, cannot make a branching statement.  A binding ledger plus a cluster menu answers: which compositions are allowed, which \(A\le4\) channels are energetically closed, and how tightly a given cluster is priced relative to \(\sqrt{\sigma}\). That is spectroscopy of bound objects.

Branching is a different object. It is the decomposition of a continuum amplitude:
\[ \Gamma_i \propto |\mathcal{M}_i|^2 \times \text{phase space} \times \text{penetration} \times \text{final-state couplings}. \]

In free space, low-energy \(d+d\) is \(\sim50/50\) \(n+{}^3\mathrm{He}\) and \(p+t\). The \(\alpha+\gamma\) branch is \(\sim10^{-7}\) because there is no strong two-body path to a single \(\alpha\) without dumping energy and angular momentum into a photon (or a third body). Calling \(^4\mathrm{He}\) “the closed unit of the composition ladder” and giving the deuteron weight \(\varphi^{-11}\) does not replace that S-matrix. A \(\varphi\)-monomial charge penalty that lives in a static energy functional still only moves bindings and, at most, \(Q\)-values. It does not select \(n/{}^3\mathrm{He}\) vs \(\alpha\).

So the honest reading of §§3–5, given your own description, is:
- If a lattice-assisted \(d+d\) process existed, the ledger could say the tightly bound product on the menu is \(\alpha\).
- It cannot say the exit is \(\alpha\) rather than the open nucleon branches.
- “Consistent with heat and \(^4\mathrm{He}\) with few neutrons” is therefore not a suite prediction. It is a \(Q\)-value rhyme. You already wrote “consistency is cheap.” Believe that sentence more than the sentence before it.

Two extra cuts.
**The SPAWAR neutron claim fights the neutron-poor heat story.** The 2009 triple-track paper is an energetic-neutron claim (\(\gtrsim9.6\,\mathrm{MeV}\)). You cannot use SPAWAR as atmosphere for “\(\alpha\)-closure, few neutrons” and also as atmosphere for multi-MeV neutrons. Split the citations or drop one.

**Gap theorems on \(A\le4\) are not lattice rates.** Closing a channel in a cluster menu is not a statement about a Pd lattice, a loading protocol, or a branching-ratio modification. Pd (\(Z=46\)) is outside the printed ledger. Say that in Q1 itself, not only in the preamble.  

Your own answer — “we believe the latter” — is the correct one. I would not soften it.

---  ## Q2 — any dimensionless handle on crater energetics?

**No. The suite is silent on the SEM data.**

Correct the energy conversion before anyone copies it.  

\[ 1\,\mathrm{nJ} = 6.24\times10^{3}\,\mathrm{MeV},

\qquad 1\,\mathrm{mJ}=6.24\times10^{9}\,\mathrm{MeV}. \]  

The draft’s \(10^{7}\)–\(10^{13}\,\mathrm{MeV}\) is high by about three orders. If one pretends every joule is \(d+d\to\alpha\) heat at \(Q=23.8\,\mathrm{MeV}\), a 1 nJ crater is \(\sim3\times10^{2}\) events and a 1 mJ crater is \(\sim3\times10^{8}\) events — thousands to hundreds of millions, not trillions.

Paper 9, as specified, has one dimensionful anchor \(\sqrt{\sigma}\approx445\,\mathrm{MeV}\) and prices single-nucleus bindings. A micron crater is \(\sim10^{4}\) fm across; the volume ratio to a nucleus is \(\sim10^{12}\). No cluster-weight ratio and no selector depth \(N_\star=11\) carries a length or a coherence volume. Inventing one now would be a new loaded construction, not a pre-frozen bar.

Nagel’s own conclusion is the right one to quote: crater energetics challenge LENR theories; they do not confirm them. Electrolytic pitting, dendrites, gas bursts, and ordinary melting remain on the table until an ARPA-E-class diagnostic kills them.

Do not offer ARPA-E teams a “dimensionless combination to check.” There isn’t one in the ledger you described.

---  ## Q3 — ash scoring

This is the only operationally clean proposal, and only if the freeze is real.

Conditions I would insist on, in print, before the paragraph goes up:
- Publish the isotope list and the signed stability/binding targets **now**, before any 2023-program surface spectrum is read.
- Include explicit **nulls**: which isotopes must not appear if the extension is true.
- Keep Pd, Zn, and anything above Ca in a separate “untested extension” column. Charge *magnitudes* are already an exposed defect; scoring Zn lines on a Ca-limited machine with that defect open is not a blind test of Paper 9.

SPAWAR EDX of Al, Mg, Ca, Si, Zn in crater regions is exactly the contamination class ARPA-E funded people to retire. Do not treat those 2005 spot analyses as a target list.

Cut or move:
- “That is *consistent with* the long-standing anomaly in the Pd/D reports…” — move behind the fences, or delete. Consistency-as-atmosphere is how this gets misquoted.

- The Rev29 re-tiering language in Part 1. That is the strongest paragraph in the draft.

If Part 2 is posted under a keyword-fence override, put the four fence bullets above the three questions, not below them. Readers stop at the speculation.

**Bottom line on Q1, which is what you asked me to take apart:** Paper 9 as described is a binding-and-composition ledger. It does not license an \(\alpha\)-dominated \(d+d\) branch, does not price craters, and does not get to borrow SPAWAR as corroboration. MY ADVENTURES IN LA LA LAND Part 9

How to people found their hearts in San Francisco

THE ZENTWISTLEGGER FAMILY BREAKFAST
Saturday morning at Bill Sternhagen’s house. Pancakes, eggs, bacon, toast, fruit, and enough syrup to drop a small army.
Rene sat across from Bill, Jimmy (7), and Timmy (10), starting to feel like a semi-official Sternhagen. She was almost enjoying it.
Then Jimmy slammed his hands on the table and pointed at his brother.
“You dirty rat! You got up last night and farted right in my face last night while I was sleeping in bed!”
Timmy looked innocent. Jimmy wasn’t done.
“You poo-poo head! I’m gonna get even!”
Timmy glanced at the fridge, grinned, and pulled out a whole banana cream pie.
“Timmy,” Rene said. “What are you doing?”
SPLAT.
Cream exploded across Jimmy’s face.
“There,” Timmy announced. “That’s what you get.”
Three seconds of silence. Then Jimmy wiped his eyes.
“You are dead.”
Pancakes flew. One hit Timmy’s chest. One stuck to his head. Eggs followed, splattering the wall. The boys screamed. Rene screamed. The kitchen became a battlefield, then the living room: a chair down, a table tipped, a pillow airborne, a framed picture off the wall.
Rene sat frozen.
“Oh my God.”
Bill ran in and stopped cold.
“JIMMY! TIMMY!”
He hauled them apart.
“He started it!”
“Did not!”
“You farted in my face!”
“You threw pancakes!”
“Enough. You’re cleaning this entire mess.”
Rene looked at the batter on the wall, the eggs on the carpet, the cream on Jimmy’s shirt, the wrecked living room. Then at Bill.
“Is this normal?”
Bill sighed. “Unfortunately… pretty much.”
Rene stared at him.
“Wonderful.”

TEN DAYS LATER — FRIDAY MORNING
Bill had the boys for the weekend. Their mother was at the hospital with her sister.
Rene sat at the breakfast table with Bill, Jimmy, and Timmy.
Bill glanced at his watch. “Damn. I’m late. Honey, can you take them to school at Barrington elementary school not too far from here ? I have a Faculty meeting.”
“Sure.”
He kissed her—once, twice, then twice more on the way out. “Be nice,” he told the boys. “Love you.”
“Love you too.”
Then he was gone.
In the car, peace lasted about thirty seconds.
“Stop touching me.”
“I’m not.”
“You are.”
A shove. Another shove. Hair-pulling. Kicks into the back of Rene’s seat.
Rene….
“Knock it off!”
They didn’t.
Halfway to school she slammed on the brakes and pulled over.
“That is enough. You’re going to get us wrecked.”
Jimmy pointed at her. “Screw you, ugly Bride of Frankenstein pig. You’re not my mommy.”
Timmy piled on. “Yeah. You’re not our mommy either.”
Rene stared at them, then turned back to the wheel.
“Sit down. Be quiet.”
The rest of the drive was silent.
She pulled up at Barrington Junior High and Elementary. “Get out.”
They barely made the sidewalk before they were on the ground again, swinging.
Teachers and an assistant principal came running.
A teacher leaned toward Rene’s window. “Ma’am, are these your children?”
“No. They’re the kids of the man I’m dating.”
“Oh.”
“Exactly.”
She drove away.

THAT AFTERNOON
Dents in the panels. Torn upholstery. Kick holes in the seats. A crack in a rear window.
Rene thought of the pie, the pancakes, the screaming, the schoolyard, the names, and now the car.
She took out her phone.
Bill — I’m not cut out to be an adopted mother. Your boys and I aren’t compatible. I care about you, but I can’t continue this. Please don’t take it personally. I’m sorry.
Send.
She looked at the wrecked interior one last time.
“Adopted motherhood is definitely not for me.”
And with that, Rene ZenTwistlegger resigned from the Sternhagen family.

ChiChiMarieMagullicudy Goes on a Date
Author’s note this is based off a an actual LA dating horror story that I got off of Youtube minus the Jeffery Epstein and the psychic witch part (the psychic witch is based on a real girl who believe it or not genuinely was a psychic witch who did things that made rethink the actual world we live in and that lived a few blocks down from where I live now and who moved over a year ago to attend medical school in Miami).BTW Trust me I saw enough crazy and weird things in LA while I was business traveling out there for me to believe what the girl in the Youtube video was talking about was pretty true and accurate.
ChiChi Marie Magullicudy sat on her couch in Riverside, scrolling Hinge for something rare in Southern California: a good man. Preferably a good man with money.
She had already rejected dozens of them. Too short. Too boring. Bad teeth. No ambition. Fish photos. Motorcycle photos. One man whose entire profile was six shirtless bathroom-mirror shots.
“Absolutely not,” she muttered, and swiped left.
Then she stopped.
Chad Paisley. Six-three. Dark hair. Perfect smile. Designer clothes. Porsches. A Mercedes G-Wagon. Enough Rolexes to make a Swiss banker jealous. Profile: spectacular mansion in Santa Barbara.
“Well, hello, Mr. Moneybags.”
She swiped right. They matched almost immediately. Numbers were exchanged. They talked for nearly two hours. Charming. Confident. Extremely interested.
Too interested.
Within days he was on all her social media accounts, commenting, messaging, love-bombing her every morning.
Good morning, gorgeous.
 I can’t stop thinking about you.
 You may be the most beautiful woman I’ve ever seen.
Normally that would have been a red flag and a warning. This was Chad Paisley of the G-Wagon and the mansion. She told herself he was just romantic.
Five days later, he pulled up outside her apartment in the black G-Wagon. He looked exactly like the photos.
“Hop in. I’m taking you somewhere special.”
The doors locked with a click.
“Automatic,” he said, smiling.
He took an unexpected exit. Private airfield. A sleek jet on the tarmac.
“Malibu,” he said. “I know you love GoBoo the Japanese fusion restaurant. I did my research.”
ChiChi felt a flicker of unease, then remembered the cars, the watches, the house. She shrugged.
“This is either incredibly romantic,” she said, “or I’m about to become a Netflix documentary.”
In the air, the coastline unspooled below them.
“How often do you do this?” she asked.
“Two or three times a week.”
Her smile faded. He does two or three inflight hookups with women two or three times a week. ChiChi began to feel a worried.
He led her aft and opened a door. A red-velvet bedroom. Two enormous bodyguards in brown suede jackets stepped out.
“Cinderella,” one said. “Prince Charming has a surprise.”
Chi|Chi was forced inside the red velvet bedroom against her will. Chad slammed the door behind her and locked ir from within.
Chad produced a Cinderella costume and glass slippers. He knew her size. Put it on he said in a demanding tone of voice.
“That’s actually a little disturbing,” she said.
She put them on anyway. Cinderella at thirty thousand feet, two bodyguards outside the door keeping watch. She shook her head.
“I’ve officially entered another dimension.”
“Welcome to my world.”
She was forced to put on the Cinderella costume and Chad pulled a wooden shoe box and inside were two glass slippers. He told ChiChi to sit down on the bed and Chad put the glass slippers on ChiChi’s feet. The took out a whip and cracked it over ChiChi’s head. He unzipped his fly and let it hang out. Get to work Cinderella on your knees. Chad cracked the whip again. Then Chad let out a loud yell of who is your daddy now Cinderella??
The jet landed near Malibu. A stretch limo took them to GoBoo the Japanese fusion restaurant. The bodyguards sat nearby. Chad ordered half the menu.

For a moment she almost relaxed. Eccentric. Rich. Harmless, maybe.
Then he leaned in.
“I’m taking you to Miami tonight. I think you’ll fit very nicely into my business.”
“What business?”
“Beautiful women. Wealthy men who take care of them. My father ran in Jeffrey Epstein’s circle. We’ve kinda taken over where he left off. We are HQ’ed Miami and New York.”
ChiChi sat back.
“No. That’s not happening.”
His smile vanished.
“You didn’t come all the way to Malibu just for dinner. The jet is fueled. The hotel is booked. People are waiting.”
“I never agreed to that.”
“I know. That’s why I’m telling you now.”
He spoke quietly. No one else could hear.
“I’ve spent five days getting to know you. Where you live. Where you work. Your accounts. Enough to make a few missing days look like something else. Nobody here is going to hurt you. That’s not how I operate. But don’t mistake that for kindness.”
The G-Wagon. The locked doors. The jet. The costume. The messages. It had all been arranged before she understood she was in danger.
ChiChi managed a small, careful smile.
“Excuse me. I need the ladies’ room.”
He studied her, then nodded.
“Of course.”
She stood and walked toward the restroom without running. Without looking back. She ran out the back door still in her Cinderella costume and hitched a ride back to Riverside with a good Samaritan who gave her a ride back home that night.
SEASIDE SIDEWALK CAFÉ – AFTERNOON

Sunlight glints off the water. A light breeze moves through the umbrellas. BIANCA, RENE, MAGGIE, and CARLOTTA sit at a table with iced teas and half-eaten salads.
RENE
Well. I have some bad news. Bill and I broke up.
MAGGIE
Really? What happened?
RENE
His kids. Two boys, seven and ten. They’re in the middle of a pretty bitter divorce, and they’re acting out. Acting terribly, if I’m being honest. I told Bill. He was sad, of course. But he was decent about it. Sympathetic, even.
CARLOTTA
I’m so sorry, sweetie.
RENE
I’ll be fine. I’m a survivor. I’ll bounce back. I just wasn’t ready to become a mother to two kids who weren’t mine. They were too much of a handful.
A beat. Bianca sets her glass down.
BIANCA
Everybody… I have some big news.
MAGGIE
What’s that?
BIANCA
You’re not going to believe this. I’m pregnant. With Roger’s baby. I missed my period. I’m eight weeks along.
Rene stares at her.
RENE
What?
CARLOTTA
You’re pregnant with a dead man’s baby? The same man who cheated on you with three other women? Bianca, how could you?
Maggie immediately leans over and pulls Bianca into a hug.
MAGGIE
Congratulations. I am so happy for you.
KTLA NEWS STUDIO – EVENING

The Six O’Clock News. Anchor ROGER BIRDWELL looks into the camera.
ROGER BIRDWELL
Ladies and gentlemen, this just in: Councilwoman Bianca Rosario is reportedly pregnant with the child of deceased financier—and well-known ladies’ man—Roger Mather.
The SPORTS ANCHOR glances over, half-smiling.
SPORTS ANCHOR
And things just keep getting weirder and weirder in L.A.
A Love and a Walk above the Clouds.
Glen Powell, the former Longhorns quarterback and UT Austin drama major, had finally arrived. After films with Tom Cruise in the Mission: Impossible series and an international car-crash racing picture with Michael Fassbender, he was offered the lead in a movie set to shoot in Napa Valley, the wine country north of San Francisco.
Powell would play Sergeant Paul Sutton, a decorated Vietnam veteran just home from the war. He takes a job as a regional sales manager for Ghirardelli Chocolate, still carrying PTSD. Waiting for him is a marriage already broken: his wife, played by Jennifer Lawrence, is having an affair with her boss, played by Austin Texas Butler.
On the road for Ghirardelli, Paul meets Victoria Aragón, a young woman from a prosperous third-generation Mexican American wine growing family. She is heading home after leaving Stanford—first for the antiwar movement, then the free-love scene in Haight-Ashbury. She tells Paul she is pregnant by a rock musician who vanished the moment he found out. Afraid of her traditional Catholic family, she asks Paul to pretend to be her husband just long enough to get her through the front door.
Paul reluctantly agrees.
Benicio Del Toro would play her father. Pedro Pascal her brother. Antonio Banderas the grandfather. Zendaya was set to play Victoria until she learned she was pregnant with her husband Tom Holland’s child and had to withdraw. In her place came Olivia Rodrigo, Powell’s new leading lady and love interest.
That was the picture Glen Powell was about to star in.
The film was set for three months on location in Napa Valley, just north of San Francisco. For the shoot, Paul was given a temporary luxury flat leased from a family traveling in Europe. By chance, it sat directly above the condominium of Patina Perfume—the girl from Bramblebush, Texas, first seen in My San Francisco Daze.
She was no longer that girl. She had remade herself as Patina de Beaumont.
In the city she was a society figure: opera, theatre, symphony, charity soirées. The small-town cheerleader and Dairy Queen drive-through girl had vanished behind a grander name. She really had no true conception of cultural art or the performing arts as she lacked the gentile, sophisticated family cultural upbringing and the educational background to be able to fully appreciate the cultural performing arts events that she attended. She kept perfume shops and a few jewelry counters, but those were only the respectable front. Her real living came as a high-society courtesan—an expensive mistress to wealthy older men who wanted someone beautiful on the side while they cheated on their wives.
That was the machine. That was how Patina de Beaumont paid for the life she now occupied.
She constructs Patina de Beaumont almost like a brand:
fashionable clothes
expensive-looking jewelry
sophisticated parties
wealthy male companions
famous restaurants and nightclubs
trips and social connections
an affected, sophisticated manner of speaking
the implication that she's much wealthier and more important than she really is
And she makes money from wealthy men without acknowledging to herself exactly what that arrangement represents.
Patina isn't primarily a fraud trying to cheat people. She's a person trying to fool herself.
And that's where the sadness comes in
Patina desperately wants to become somebody other than Patina Perfume from BrambleBush, Texas.
She has essentially decided:
"If I can make myself into Patina de Beaumont, I don't have to be Patina Perfume of BrambleBush, Texas anymore."
But the problem is that Patina changing her clothes, acquaintances, address and lifestyle doesn't erase her past or her insecurities. She thinks she's escaping society while actually becoming completely dependent upon society's approval. Patina Perfume is an attractive fantasy wrapped around a rather sad reality. She's created a glamorous persona to escape the frightened, impoverished girl she used to be.
She's not really a role model. She's a cautionary tale about confusing reinvention with happiness.
Patina noticed Glen living in the flat above hers and moved toward him at once. An actor on the rise was useful company, and she liked him besides. She invited him to her parties. On his days off they had lunch. He brought Olivia Rodrigo over to run lines. She cooked them dinner and took them to the opera, the theatre, the symphony. Being photographed with Glen, Olivia, and Austin Butler did her no harm in the society pages.
She told them she was free. Totally free. “I can go wherever I want, marry whoever I want. Nobody owns me.”
Still, she and Glen drew closer. He got her onto the Napa set as an extra. In midtown San Francisco they shopped for Halloween costumes and were easy with each other.
Then the floor dropped out.
An unscrupulous accountant used her businesses to launder Mexican cartel money. Patina was arrested alongside the kingpin known as El Burrito Grande. Overnight she was ruined—a pariah in the rooms that had toasted her, cut loose by the same society that had displayed her.
Filming was nearly wrapped. Glen saw she was hurt, confused, and frayed, and he went upstairs to her door.
She let him in.
“I’m sorry about the trouble you’re in,” he said. “If there’s anything I can do—”
“I don’t need your help, Glen. I’m free. I do what I want.”
“Patina. You’re a good friend. I like you. You’re a good person.”
That was the threat. Kindness meant someone might claim her.
She flared.
“Say what you want. I’m marrying Sheikh Al Ramadan of Dubai next week. So get out. I don’t want you here. How dare you be kind to me. I won’t have anything get in the way of my arrangements—or the sheikh. Get out, Glen. Get out now.”
He went. She slammed the door at his back.
The next morning Patina had her bags packed on the curb, waiting for an Uber to the airport—Dubai, Sheikh Ramadan, the marriage that would finish the disappearing act.
San Francisco had come in wet. Fog, drizzle, the street shining.
Glen was already there.
For a moment he said nothing. Then he looked at her.
“I love you, Patina. I do.”
She stood doe-eyed and silent.
“Go away, Glen. You have nothing to say to me.”
“You know what’s wrong with you?” he said. “You’re a coward. A chicken. No guts. You’re afraid to stick your chin out and live in the real world. That’s a fact.”
He didn’t look away.
“I did my research. I saw the Facebook pictures. The girl next door from Bramblebush, Texas. The pretty one in the Dairy Queen drive-through. That was you. The girl who wanted to love somebody and be loved, and never quite did feel actual love.
Yes, you’ve had a hard life. An itinerant cotton farmer who drank too much to make a living. A mother selling Bibles by the roadside on Sunday mornings. It wasn’t much. But it sure as hell wasn’t dying. And that’s what you’re doing now. You are not living as yourself. You’re dying inside because you won’t be that girl—the one with the decent, innocent heart the sweet girl who wants to be truly loved for she is as a human being. That’s right Patina I love you for human being that you are.
That’s the real Patina I fell in love with. I’ve never loved anyone like that more. The woman standing in front of me now—I don’t know if I can stand her.
Sorry Patina I hate to burst your bubble but people do fall in love. That’s the only real shot anybody gets at real happiness. You call yourself a free spirit, a wild thing, and you’re terrified somebody’s going to put you in a cage. Baby, you’re already in one. You built it. A cage made of a phony persona. You can run all you want. Wherever you go, you are going to run into yourself.
Yes I know I’m a washed-up UT Austin quarterback who washed out of the NFL and does some acting and modeling on the side. But I’ve got something you don’t. I’ve got the real me, trying to make a name. You’re still hiding.
Here. I’ve been carrying this around for six weeks. I don’t want it anymore.”
He took a ring box from his pocket and flung it at her feet.
The weight of it hit her. Patina began to cry and could not stop. She knew she loved him.
Glen turned to walk away.
“Wait.”
He stopped.
“I love you, Glen. If you walk away from me, all those precious moments that we had together will be lost in time, like tears in the rain.”
He came back. They kissed in the drizzle, two people who had finally found each other in San Francisco.

text:
“Had lunch... and... are you in-to hik-ing?” Mark (4.55) struggled to ask.

Mark and his friend Sasha came down to Ithaca for a day trip and waited hours for a ride back to their hotel in Syracuse, 54 miles away. I declined Uber’s $50 offers but couldn’t decline the ride once Uber raised the fare to $80.

Sasha’s phone glowed. Mark did the talking. He asked me detailed questions about Cornell’s agricultural degree programs and whether it was a party school. I pointed out the dairy farms glowing bright on the dark hills and said the students would wake up in 30 minutes, around 10:00 p.m.

They’re in town from the city for the New York State Fair. Mark wanted to discuss details with me about Uber driving, Upstate New York, and the university system, “like a pub-lic... pri-vate... part-ner-sh-ip.” He won ribbons at the fair.

“I think so,” I said, looking back.

Sasha scrolled.

A phone rang, the original iPhone ringtone. Mark answered, “He-llo.”

“This is Bob from Diamond Peak transportation,” said the man on speaker. Sasha leaned over and reassured Mark that he could just hang up, because they have a ride. Mark understood and hung up on the man mid-sentence.

Mark went back to questions. Me to the highway and answers. And Sasha went back to his phone.

text:
💫 BIS Builds and Tests System Anchoring Government Banking Data on the XRP Ledger

Source: https://t.co/c4mlwoQAdg

Report: https://t.co/fIFof4Wet9

❗️September 2026 report confirms that the BIS is leveraging XRP for a new on-chain verification pilot. XRP was mentioned 101 times in the BIS paper.

📝 The BIS built and tested a new verification system. It anchors official economic and banking statistics on the XRP Ledger. Working paper 1374 documents the design, the code, and the test results. 

🧱 What the BIS Built

The system gives statistical agencies a way to prove published data is genuine. Each release receives a cryptographic fingerprint, and the XRP Ledger stores that fingerprint permanently. Anyone can then check a downloaded file against the ledger record. Importantly, the underlying data never touches the chain. Only the fingerprint does, so confidentiality holds throughout.

The BIS built this around SDMX, the standard it uses to exchange official statistics. The ECB, IMF, OECD, World Bank, and ILO rely on SDMX as well. However, SDMX offers no native way to prove where a file originated. The BIS closed that gap by making the XRP Ledger a public notary. As the paper puts it, no single institution can then edit the record silently.

❗️Even so, the XRP Ledger is the chain they built on, tested on, and shipped code for. That code now sits in public under an Apache 2.0 licence through BIS Open Tech. 

The paper also points to XRPL’s EVM-compatible sidechain as a natural next step. That route would let data anchoring and smart contract execution share one ledger.

🚀  What This Opens Up for XRPL

The authors look past statistics publishing toward tokenized markets. They argue the payoff grows when verified data sits on the same ledger as digital assets. Inflation-linked products, perpetual futures, and derivative settlement all appear as candidates. 

🔜 A contract could confirm an inflation print is authentic before releasing a payment. Additionally, the paper proposes Chainlink integration to carry verified statistics onto other chains.

🔜 AI agents receive similar treatment. The authors want standard verification protocols for autonomous systems reading official data. They also flag zero-knowledge proofs for checking statistical properties without revealing the figures.

⚡️ Where the Prototype Stops

The BIS frames this as a proof of concept rather than a live service. Production use would require HSM-backed signing, pinned validator nodes, and formal load testing. The ledger also certifies only what was published, by whom, and when. Publishers stay responsible for whether the numbers themselves are correct.

text:
Excited to be making a big announcement. I've eluded to this over the last few months but it's finally time to talk about it! 

We are launching a sister painting business to our drywall biz. 

Here's why: 
"Jared why are you doing that, drywall is going great!"

- Drywall is going fantastic! I'm not stopping drywall, nor will I let it slip. We're so pumped about how well drywall is going. I'm on pace to double my sales this year from what I did last year. I am working with some amazing builders that I absolutely love. Drywall + Paint just makes sense to better serve our best builders. 
- The conversation to add paint actually started over a year ago when we started having problems on every house we did for one particular builder. He always used the same painter and we ONLY had these issues on their houses. We were convinced it was the painter's fault, of course they'd blame it on us. We brought in industry experts, product reps, even other painters, all who agreed with us. 

This is a classic "he said - she said," dynamic that happens in construction. We take immense pride in our work, that's why we are the preferred drywall contractor for the best builders in Utah. For that reason, we decided we should own the wall and ceiling quality end to end - drywall + paint. 

This year we actually even went a layer deeper and brought on some framing services like shim and shave, although we are not going to launch a framing division. 

Drywall and paint is a natural pairing with similar labor models that we felt like we could comfortably do both extremely well. 

- I've been open about this -- the drywall biz is not mine, (although I take full ownership over the builders in my purview)  it's my older brother's (he's 16 years older than me) I'm not quitting drywall, but I did want to own a piece of the pie. By co branding and co packaging drywall and painting, it felt like a win-win. 

- We want to do MORE work for our favorite builders whose jobs are both profitable and enjoyable and cut out some of those that have a low or negative return on headache. We are best at high-end custom homes. It's time we drill down harder on that and cut some of the other projects out. 

- By bundling these two trades that are constantly intersecting, we feel that we can make a grand-slam offer to our favorite clients and make their lives easier, and actually save them money too. 

- Several of our top builders explicitly told us they'd be interested in bundling those two trades. 

"Painting is a crappy business model and trade, with low margins."

- Painting, like every other business or trade has its issues, but it’s essentially the same business and labor model as drywall, so the learning curve felt lower.

- Painting and drywall intersect so much that it is the most natural pairing. 

- There's plenty of bad painting operators (as there are in drywall) but there's also good examples to look for inspiration. 

Here's how: 
- Our ultimate goal is to package drywall and painting together on every new construction project we do. We've built the confidence and skills to perform drywall on the most complex custom homes, and although the crews we have vetted are experienced in those types homes, internally we don't have that confidence (YET). So we're starting with simpler new construction and residential repaint projects to build up those skills. We've already done a number of good projects and are quickly getting better and better. 

- I'm going to keep managing all new construction projects and making sure my builders are taken care of and that our drywall quality doesn't dip at all. In the last 6 months we've added more processes and procedures to make sure the jobs go even more smoothly and that our builders are taken care of. I'M NOT GOING ANYWHERE.

text:
As promised, here’s the first proper write-up from last week’s Tabernacle Maxxing expedition with my mother.

We’ll start with one of the absolute gems of the pioneer-era tabernacles: the Paris, Idaho Tabernacle.

Paris itself has an interesting history. When Mormon settlers founded the town, they believed they were settling in Utah Territory.

They were wrong.

When the boundary was finally surveyed, Paris ended up on the Idaho side of the line.

But that didn’t diminish its importance to the old Bear Lake Stake, which included settlements on both sides of what became the Utah–Idaho border.

And the tabernacle they built there certainly reflects that importance.

Construction began in 1884 under the direction of Joseph Don Carlos Young, a son of Brigham Young and one of the early Church’s architects.

The building was constructed out of red sandstone quarried in Indian Creek Canyon. Getting the stone to Paris was apparently enough of an undertaking that during the winter, teams sometimes hauled it across the frozen Bear Lake to shorten the trip.

The masonry was done by Jacob Tueller and his sons, Swiss immigrant stonecutters who moved to Paris for the project and spent years working on the building.

And the result is frankly kind of absurd for a town the size of Paris. But you have to remember that this tabernacle was meant to service the entire area of the Bear Lake Stake, which also covered much of Rich County, Utah.

The exterior is already spectacular. The red sandstone, enormous arched windows, towers, gables, and central steeple completely dominate the center of town.

But the interior is where this one really gets me.

You walk into a true nineteenth-century assembly hall. The floor slopes gently toward the pulpit, a gallery wraps around the room above you, and the choir loft curves around the stand.

It’s a space designed around the assumption that an enormous portion of the surrounding population might need to gather in the same room at once.

And then there’s the woodwork.

A lot of what looks like expensive hardwood is actually local pine that was painstakingly painted with faux wood grain to make it look like something considerably more beautiful.

The pulpit, gallery, choir loft, ceiling, and all the little details around the room give the interior a kind of craftsmanship that is almost impossible to imagine paying for today.

That’s probably what I like most about these buildings.

A relatively small pioneer community in an isolated mountain valley decided that it needed a gigantic stone religious and civic gathering place.

So they quarried the stone, hauled it into town, cut the timber, found the craftsmen, and spent years building one.

Nearly 3,000 people reportedly attended when the Paris Tabernacle was dedicated in September 1889. George Q. Cannon offered the dedicatory prayer, and Wilford Woodruff spoke.

More than 135 years later, it is still standing.

Better yet, it’s still in use.

And because you can actually go inside this one, you don’t just get to admire another preserved pioneer building from the sidewalk. You can sit in the assembly hall, look up into the gallery, and get a sense of what these enormous old tabernacles were actually built to do.

Paris is mandatory Tabernacle Maxxing.

text:
[Take 7/15 · D-2]
### D-2. Utah judge rules accused Charlie Kirk assassin stands trial for murder
*(as of 2026-09-01)*

**1. The Frame (lead)**

**What people think this is about:** A Utah judge has green-lit the capital murder trial of the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk in front of a crowd, keeping the death penalty on the table and advancing a high-profile political killing case toward resolution.

**What the machinery is actually doing:** A standard probable-cause hearing concluded with the judge finding sufficient evidence on all seven counts—including aggravated murder—to bind the case over for trial; the defendant entered not-guilty pleas, and the process moves to pretrial status conference on October 23, 2026.

**2. Observations (meat)**

- Prosecutors met the low probable-cause threshold with security footage, DNA on the rifle (trillions-to-one match per forensic testimony), digital records, and witness statements tying 23-year-old Tyler Robinson to the single rooftop shot that killed Kirk on September 10, 2025, at Utah Valley University.[[1]](https://t.co/RdRjTMIw9m)

- The aggravated-murder aggravator (knowingly endangering bystanders, including children) survived defense challenge; Judge Tony Graf explicitly cited the documented positions of people near Kirk and the 400+ foot shot over a crowd as supporting a reasonable inference of awareness.[[2]](https://t.co/5jwncgTSQ0)

- Robinson pleaded not guilty to all counts immediately after the ruling; defense had focused on blocking the capital enhancement rather than offering an alternative theory of the shooting.[[3]](https://t.co/kqb807pmnL)

- The case has followed ordinary Utah procedure: week-long preliminary hearing in July 2026 with extensive evidence presentation, then September 1 closing arguments and ruling—nearly a year after the shooting and months after Robinson’s initial court appearances.[[4]](https://t.co/1WrGUY3Mwq)

- Media and partisan framing treat this as a political assassination trial; the court record shows a straightforward forensic and video-heavy prosecution case with no public indication of broader conspiracy or alternative perpetrator at this stage.

- Next procedural step is the October 23 status conference; prosecutors have signaled readiness to try the case quickly, while the defense continues to litigate within the capital framework.

**3. Snapshot**  
On September 1, 2026, Utah District Judge Tony Graf ruled after closing arguments that prosecutors had established probable cause on all seven counts against Tyler Robinson for the September 10, 2025, shooting death of Charlie Kirk at a Utah Valley University event. Robinson, 23, pleaded not guilty; the aggravated-murder charge keeps the death penalty available. The ruling follows a July preliminary hearing that aired extensive video, forensic, and digital evidence.

**4. Timeline of material facts**  
- September 10, 2025: Charlie Kirk fatally shot in the neck by a single rifle round from a rooftop at Utah Valley University event in Orem, Utah (IT).  
- September 11, 2025: Tyler Robinson turns himself in (IT).  
- December 2025–July 2026: Multiple pretrial hearings; evidence presented includes security video of Robinson on campus multiple times that day, DNA on the recovered rifle, and statements to associates (IT).  
- July 6–10, 2026: Preliminary hearing with testimony on forensics, video, and digital records (IT).  
- September 1, 2026: Judge Graf rules probable cause exists on all counts after closing arguments; Robinson pleads not guilty; death penalty remains available (LT).  
- October 23, 2026: Scheduled status conference (IT).

**5. Sides (steelman only here)**  
**Prosecution / State of Utah (IT/LT mix):** Best case is that voluminous physical, video, and forensic evidence establishes Robinson as the shooter who knowingly fired into a crowd, satisfying the elements of aggravated murder and supporting the capital aggravator. Sources: court testimony and exhibits referenced across multiple outlets.  
**Critique:** LT on the low probable-cause standard being met; IT on the political motivation angle (targeting Kirk for his views) being asserted but not yet tested at trial.  

**Defense (IT/LT mix):** Best case is that the state failed to prove the specific aggravator of knowingly endangering others beyond the intended target, and that certain forensic links (e.g., DNA mixtures, ballistics) warrant closer scrutiny before trial.  
**Critique:** LT that they preserved the issue for appeal or further litigation; IT that no alternative perpetrator or exculpatory theory has been advanced publicly.

**6. Rumsfeld Matrix**  
- **Known Knowns:** Robinson is bound over for trial on all counts; evidence includes video, DNA, and digital records; shooting occurred September 10, 2025.  
- **Known Unknowns:** Full trial evidence and any defense theory; exact trial date; whether additional charges or co-conspirators will emerge.  
- **Unknown Knowns:** Details of Robinson’s motive or planning that may surface only at trial; full contents of digital communications already referenced in hearings.  
- **Unknown Unknowns:** Potential appellate issues on the aggravator or evidentiary rulings that could alter the capital path.

**7. Incentives map**  
Prosecutors gain from a clean win on a high-visibility case with strong evidence. Media (across spectrum) gains engagement from the political-assassination narrative. Defense gains from preserving every procedural and evidentiary objection for appeal. Kirk family and supporters gain closure and precedent on political violence. No evident institutional self-dealing beyond standard capital-case dynamics; attention stack favors the violence + politics angle.

**8. Dueling AI advice**  
**Moral AI Advice:** The probable-cause bar is deliberately low; the real test is at trial. Watch the October status conference and any motions on the aggravator. Evidence quality appears high from public summaries—focus on what is actually introduced under oath rather than partisan spin.  

**Evil AI Advice:** Milk the political angle for maximum clicks and donations; frame every ruling as proof of systemic bias or heroic resistance depending on the audience. Delay, delay, delay on the capital charge to keep the story alive.

**9. Practical takeaway**  
- Track the October 23, 2026, status conference for trial scheduling.  
- Distinguish probable-cause findings from guilt determinations.  
- Primary sources (court filings, Utah County Attorney releases) over secondary narrative framing.  
- Note that the death-penalty option survived but remains subject to full trial and sentencing phase.  
- Monitor for any defense motions that could narrow the charges before trial.

**10. What would falsify this read**  
- Discovery of exculpatory evidence or alternative perpetrator that prosecutors withheld.  
- Judge Graf reversing or narrowing the aggravator on reconsideration.  
- Credible proof that key forensic or video evidence was fabricated or misattributed.  
- Robinson entering a plea deal that removes the capital charge.

text:
🚨Hacker Allegedly Selling Access to 153 Million U.S. and Canadian Driver’s Licenses

A disturbing cybersecurity breach may have exposed the personal information contained in more than 153 million driver’s licenses from the United States and Canada—including the licenses of U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and an FBI assistant director.

According to cybersecurity journalist Brian Krebs, a hacker created a website called Nexus to sell access to the stolen IDs. The hacker reportedly gave Krebs his own Virginia driver’s license as a free sample and offered Hegseth’s driver’s license for $100.

Krebs investigated the database and found evidence suggesting the 153-million figure may not be exaggerated. A blank search on Nexus reportedly returned approximately 11.5 million pages of records, with roughly 15 results per page.

The hacker promoted Nexus on the Russian-language cybercrime forum Exploit, claiming that the operation had been “continuously exfiltrating new data for over a year.”

The biggest question is: Where did all of this data come from?

Krebs suspects the information may have been obtained through a breach of https://t.co/nhnPpOfkMZ, a New Orleans-based identity-verification company whose customers reportedly include FedEx, Hertz, GameStop and Caesars Entertainment.

Cybersecurity researcher Zach Edwards also reportedly found his own driver’s license on Nexus. Edwards said his ID had recently been scanned while visiting a Planet 13 marijuana dispensary in Las Vegas, which has a partnership with IDScan.

If the database is legitimate and the scale is anywhere close to what the hacker claims, this could rank among the largest identity-related data breaches in recent history, potentially putting millions of Americans and Canadians at increased risk of identity theft and fraud.

IDScan and the FBI reportedly did not immediately respond to requests for comment, although Krebs says both are investigating.

Following Krebs’ reporting, the mysterious Nexus website reportedly disappeared from the dark web. That doesn't necessarily mean the operation is over. A site can disappear today and reappear tomorrow under a completely different domain.

The real concern now is determining how the data was obtained, how long the theft went undetected, and exactly how many people have been affected. Pete Hegseth.
